DETAILS

1.10 2026-11-26 Print routine, SQL sanitation, and some POD corrections

-   Changed Getopt::Long endpoint parameter to endpoint=s the
    END_(POINT) and APHIA_(NS) setting in the tool will be removed
-   Changed the endpoint protocol from http to https.
-   Changed the CVS & SQL quoting mechanism to prevent SQL injection.
-   ADVISE: The program produces SQL output and has no DBI connection.
    Asserting propper field within the WoRMS DB in terms of QA is not
    provided!
-   The print routine for SQL, CSV and plain TEXT output was reviewed.
-   The AI gives none conform POD formatting advises for =head1 standard
    entries. Never trust the reformatted crap the machine produces.
-   Version removed from the POD because shipped by dzil
-   POD default variables collected in section DEFAULT SETTINGS

1.9 2026-11-26 POD synopsis and some CPAN dzil adjustments

-   Split the DESCRIPTION and SYNOPSIS sections of the POD, code example
    added to SYNOPSIS
-   Automationg CHANGELOG and SECURITY from meta/Changes.org and
    meta/Security.org via dzil and pandoc (central source point)
-   Testing manpage production

1.8 2026-11-25 POD corrections and improve test coverage

-   Restructure headlines add experimental functions
-   Added tests for then SOAP configuration
-   Add tests for the output formats and and taxon child entries

1.7 2026-11-24 POD corrections

-   Add two tests for a better CPAM Tester Matrix integration
-   Play around with dzil smoke –author –release
-   Left C<…> POD formatting which looks ugly in MetaCPAN
-   Flag MetaCPAN backlog for Pause account integration

1.6 2026-11-24 Expressive library description towards WoRMS

-   Change the POD NAME to WoRMS access aspects for better CPAN listing
-   Remove `C<…>` formatting from `=item …` for better CSS rendering

1.5 2026-08-07 POD formatting and typo's

-   add code and link formatting rules for WoRMS.pm and query-worms.
-   catch typo's ..spellchecker
-   try to understand the module application realation for POD links

1.4 2026-07-28 CPAN Deployment Changelog

-   collection info from 2012 to 2026 to have a consistent log
-   generate a minimal changelog (ORG)
-   transferring it via pandoc

1.3 2026-07-28 CPAN Deployment Corrections (substantial)

-   flagging [ExeDir] in DIZL
-   flagging [autoprerecq] to add used modules
-   managing [ReadmeFromPod]

1.2 2026-07-27 CPAN Deployment Corrections (technical)

-   fighting the DZIL configuration madness
-   add a full in line POD to lib/Net/WoRMS.pm
-   change the abstract line

1.1 2026-07-27 CPAN Deployment

-   renaming the tool to bin/query-worms
-   pin minimal Perl version v5.20
-   switch to modern Perl syntax (signatures) keyword (match-case)
-   moved away form pure github.com published repo towards Dist::Zilla
-   add the module Net::WoRMS for abstraction and maintainability in
    lib/Net/WoRMS.pm
-   re-factor the CLI via Getopt::Long and Net::WoRMS
-   remove the buggy find-fuzzy task
-   add a full POD for bin/query-worms

1.0 2017-08-01 Published Version for Github

-   publihed under bigopensky/web-harvester/worms-harvester.pl at github
-   cleaned mode selector via switch statement
-   minimal POD was added
-   licensing issues addessed und GPL/3

0.1 2012-03-12 Initial release

Initial release to track an correct taxa for the Benthos database of the
Institute for Applied Ecology (IfAÖ).

#@ I4W

0.09  2026-11-27
    - Fix: slimpack exits with an error, and writes nothing, when the
      script does not compile. It used to write an incomplete bundle and
      exit 0, e.g. when a module the script uses was not installed.
    - Fix: the trace sees the --lib directory, as the bundle does, so a
      script that needs it to compile is traced fully.

0.08  2026-10-21
    - Fix: require Module::CoreList 3.07; on perls <= 5.16 the core-shipped
      version has no is_core() and slimpack died with "Undefined subroutine".
    - Fix: names referenced from non-interpolating strings (q[...], '...',
      <<'EOT') are no longer renamed — such strings can be string-eval'd at
      runtime. Bundling Moo broke on perl < 5.22 (Sub::Defer builds deferred
      subs from a q[...] template naming its lexicals, a sub and its package).
    - Fix: keep the space in `$x && Foo::Bar->baz` and `$n - word(...)`;
      removing it warns on perl <= 5.18 ("Operator or semicolon missing") or
      turns `- e(...)` into a filetest.
    - Fix: -e/-E bundles failed on perl < 5.16 (no ':all' feature bundle
      there; those perls now get ':5.10').

0.07  2026-10-19
    - Fix: perl -c on a packed script no longer runs the program.

0.06  2026-10-19
    - New: compressed sources are stored as escaped binary, about 25% smaller.
      Use --no-binary for a plain-text (base64) bundle that survives diff,
      mail and copy-paste.
    - New: a boot program's __DATA__/__END__ section is compressed too, read
      through an in-memory DATA handle; it is no longer left verbatim with a
      warning.
    - Fix: bundling a program with no modules produced a syntax error.
    - New: the bundle keeps the boot script's shebang line; without one it
      gets #!/usr/bin/env perl, so bundles run on systems without
      /usr/bin/perl (e.g. FreeBSD). --shebang LINE overrides it.
    - Fix: the test suite ran bundles through their shebang and failed on
      machines without /usr/bin/perl; it now uses the perl running the tests.
    - Fix: embedded sources could use `;` as a q-literal delimiter, which is
      a syntax error on perl 5.16 and older.

0.05  2026-10-19
    - Minifier moved to its own module, App::SlimPacker::Minify.
    - New: rename sub and method names across the whole bundle
      (--rename-subs, on by default). Names Perl looks up by string
      (builtins, new, DESTROY, tie/serialization methods, can('...')) are kept.
    - New: rename bundled package names (--rename-modules, on by default),
      e.g. App::Foo::UI becomes bk::bl::UI.
    - New: rename subs in import/export lists and can() strings
      (--rename-exports, on by default).
    - New: --include and --exclude add modules to the bundle or leave them out.
    - --rename-vars is the new name for --rename (old name still works).
    - Moo programs no longer bundle Moose unless they use it.
    - ALL_CAPS lexicals (my $ROWS) are now renamed too.
    - Variables interpolated in regexes (qr/\Q$query\E/) are now renamed.
    - Plugins are inlined before renaming, so they get renamed consistently.
    - Fix: ternaries with a bareword branch were mistaken for labels.
    - Fix: --bundle-lib-all could drop the main program from the output.
    - Fix: module-only renaming could break "$Pkg::var" strings.
    - Fix: Moo programs failed to run when bundled with sub or module renaming.
    - Fix: XS modules keep their package names, so their compiled code loads.

0.04  2026-09-07
    - Compression is on by default: bundled modules and the main program are
      deflated and decompressed on load (core modules only).
      Use --no-compress to keep the sources readable.
    - New: --rewrite (opt-in, experimental) shortens code, e.g.
      foreach -> for, $x += 1 -> $x++, print($x) -> print $x.
    - --rewrite renames our globals across the whole bundle, including
      inside interpolated strings and heredocs.
    - Smaller bundles: embedded sources are quoted more compactly.
    - All on/off options accept a --no-* form.
    - Fix: __END__/__DATA__ could merge with the surrounding lines and
      lose the data section.

0.03  2026-09-05
    - New: minify-only mode (slimpack minify FILE, or the minify script).
    - Faster: each module is parsed once instead of twice.
    - Shebang lines are kept when minifying.

0.02  2026-09-05
    - Only my variables are renamed; local/our globals are left alone.
    - Modules without a .packlist are found in @INC.
    - Core modules are never bundled.
    - Fix: minifier broke print $fh $$source.

0.01  2026-09-04
    - Initial release.

         "changes_file" : "Changes",
         "changes_text" : "Revision history for Mail::DKIM2

0.36    2026-11-28
        dkim2-milter, from an originating host's report (thanks, Al
        Iverson):
        - Outbound mode stamps m=1 from the message itself when there is
          no snapshot store. 0.35 computed a Message-Instance only with
          --snapshot-dir, so a host that just sends its own mail never
          signed ("no Message-Instance field to sign over").
        - --mode both now decides each transaction by where the message
          comes from, as OpenDKIM does: outbound (signed) for a client on
          loopback or a unix socket (Postfix gives non_smtpd_milters
          127.0.0.1), one that authenticated ({auth_authen}), or one in
          the new --internal-hosts; inbound (verified, stamped, never
          signed) for anything else. 0.35 verified and signed in the same
          transaction: with --snapshot-dir (the shipped
          dkim2-milter.service) a locally sent message was signed over a
          second m=1 with an A-R inserted after signing, permerror at
          every receiver; and mail from outside with a From in one of our
          domains would have been signed. One both socket now also serves
          a list host: the post is snapshotted on arrival and the list's
          re-injected copy diffed against it.
        - New --authserv-id for the Authentication-Results it adds
          (default still "localhost").
        - --help documents --mode and --authserv-id, and no longer lists
          --verify/--no-verify and --sign/--no-sign, which never existed.
          The "verify only" SYNOPSIS example now passes --mode inbound
          (without it the milter refused to start with no key).
        - POD: an originating-host Postfix setup; deploy/examples/ has
          dkim2-milter-originating.service.

0.35    2026-11-16
        Security: three faults reported against 0.34.
        - CVE-2026-129847: a line in the header section that is not a
          header field (no colon; white space or nothing before the
          colon; a fold before the colon, which RFC 5322 does not allow
          and 0.34 read as a field; a first line starting with white
          space) was dropped unread, so it was in no header hash: such
          lines could be added to a signed message without breaking any
          Message-Instance, while other parsers read them (Python's email
          ends the header section at one). The Verifier now gives
          "PERMERROR: malformed header field" for a message with any
          DKIM2 field, before every other check, and the Signer refuses
          ("malformed header field"). A message with no DKIM2 field is
          still none. New HeaderParser method malformed_header. Since
          0.22.
        - CVE-2026-129848: the tag-list parser trimmed a value's trailing
          white space with a pattern quadratic in a run of white space
          inside the value: a DKIM2-Signature or Message-Instance field
          of about 1MB took minutes, before any authentication. Linear
          now; what is accepted is unchanged. Since 0.20.
        - CVE-2026-129849: Mail::DKIM2::Validate::report walked the chain
          level by level even when the Verifier had refused it for having
          more than 32 Message-Instance or DKIM2-Signature fields, parsing
          the whole message again at every level: one request to the
          validator could cost minutes. Over the limit it now reports the
          Verifier's PERMERROR and no levels; it reads i= and m= only as
          chain numbers (1 to 99). Since 0.18.

0.34    2026-11-15
        - dkim2-milter: the inbound milter takes a snapshot (and stamps an
          instance, and wraps) only when the chain verified or there was
          none, and that snapshot is the outbound milter's proof of it. A
          message whose X-DKIM2-Snapshot token names a snapshot of it is
          signed without its upstream signatures being verified again:
          only the Message-Instance fields are checked, with no key
          lookups. The snapshot has to be of that message (the same
          DKIM2-Signature fields and the instances they cover), or the
          message is not signed. With no snapshot, everything is verified
          before signing, as before.
        - dkim2-milter: the inbound milter adds X-DKIM2-Arrival with its
          verdict as one word. The outbound milter does not sign a message
          that arrived fail, permerror or temperror (550 5.7.1 if it has a
          DKIM2-Signature on it, as for any refusal). The field is removed
          on sight by every mode, so it neither comes from outside nor
          leaves the host; an inbound milter with --no-envelope-check
          keeps a failing verdict the milter before it gave, and behind a
          pass or none takes a Message-Instance nobody has signed for
          this host's own (the m=1 the first milter stamped on an unsigned
          post) instead of reporting permerror.
        - Mail::DKIM2::Hop->snapshot_vouches($message, $snapshot): whether
          a snapshot is of this very message.
        - A message handed over as a string Perl holds as characters is
          hashed as the octets those characters stand for. With the
          OpenSSL digests (the default wherever Net::SSLeay is installed)
          it was hashed as the string's UTF-8, so a Message-Instance
          computed for such a message, if it had an octet above 0x7F in
          it, did not match the octets sent. Email::MIME gives a character
          string once any one header field of it has been upgraded. A
          string with a character above 0xFF croaks ("Wide character"),
          as it did with the CryptX digests.

0.33    2026-11-14
        - A From field value longer than 2048 octets (not counting the line
          breaks of folding or the white space round it) is not read for a
          mailbox: from_mailbox gives 'none', so the Verifier's result is
          "matching From is not authentic" and the Signer does not sign.
          $Mail::DKIM2::Address::MAX_FROM_LENGTH holds the limit. Every
          implementation in the interop repository now has it; one of
          them took tens of seconds to parse a hostile 100 KB From.
        - The Verifier waits no longer than 20 seconds in all for one
          message's DNS lookups ($Mail::DKIM2::Verifier::LOOKUP_BUDGET):
          after that the lookups not yet made fail at once, and the result
          is temperror, as for any DNS failure. A message can name 8 keys
          per signature and 32 signatures, each lookup worth the
          resolver's whole timeout. Lookups made by a PubkeyCallback or a
          PolicyCallback are not counted.

0.32    2026-11-14
        - dkim2-milter and the DKIM2Sign handler sign a message that has a
          List-Id header field with the exploded flag (-09 section 12.5),
          whether or not it carries the X-DKIM2-Exploded hint: a list sent
          it, to more than one address. A stock Mailman list, which adds
          no hint, went out without the flag. Never on a first signature,
          as before.

0.31    2026-11-14
        (0.31 was prepared on 2026-11-06 and never released; this is that
        work and the clean-up that followed it.)

        The clean-up: no change to the wire format, to what verifies, or to
        any result string. What a caller may notice:

        - Signer: the Algorithm defaults to the one the key signs with (it
          was rsa-sha256 whatever the key, and an Ed25519 key then died
          inside CLOSE). An Algorithm the library does not implement, or
          one the key cannot sign with, croaks from new(): before, any name
          not starting "ed25519" produced an RSA signature labelled with
          that name.
        - Signer: an RSA key under 1024 bits does not sign (-09 section
          3.2): result 'fail', details "signing key is shorter than 1024
          bits". Every verifier already called such a signature "too
          short".
        - Signer: a message carrying a Message-Instance with no m= is
          refused, as every verifier refuses it.
        - Verifier: new AcceptedAt option, the time the message was accepted
          over SMTP, for a caller verifying later than that: t= is checked
          against it instead of now (-09 section 14.3).
        - Verifier: provisionally_verified() checks the envelope against the
          top signature's mf= and rt= when the Verifier was given one
          (MailFrom, RcptTo; -09 section 13.2 step 4). It was skipped.
        - Verifier: the StreamBody option and stream_body() are gone. The
          chain is always checked from the header and body plans; the undo
          walk it could be switched back to is now only the tests'
          reference (t/lib/UndoWalkVerifier.pm). HeadersOnly reads its one
          hash from the plan too, and the Verifier no longer loads
          Email::MIME.
        - MessageInstance: a calculated null body Recipe is unrecoverable()
          as a parsed one is (it was false until the field was re-parsed).
        - MessageInstance: a parsed instance's as_string writes every hash
          group it was given (it wrote only the sha256 set).
        - MessageInstance: UseEpilogue and EpilogueThreshold, which croaked
          since 0.23, are removed (unknown options now), with dkim2-milter's
          --use-epilogue and --epilogue-threshold. calculate never changes
          the message it is given.
        - MessageInstance: the h1/b1 entries of get_tag are gone;
          header_hash() and body_hash() remain, and take an algorithm.
        - Common: build_signing_input takes the fields themselves
          (instances, signatures, signing) and empties the s= values of the
          one being signed or checked. The Signer and the Verifier now
          build the input the same way; the Verifier no longer re-serialises
          the parsed signature. Signature::as_string_without_data and
          as_folded_string_without_data are gone with it.
        - Common: a Message-Instance or DKIM2-Signature field written with
          white space before its colon is canonicalized for the signing
          input without it (-09 section 12.8).
        - Common: digest64 and fold_value (unused) are gone, and so is
          HeaderPlan::rewrites_instances (see the security fix below: it
          could only ever be false).
        - Deprecated, still working, to be removed: Common::extract_domain
          (use domain_of) and Gate's AllowNullBodyRecipe (a no-op since
          0.29).

        New:

        - Mail::DKIM2::Chain: a message's Message-Instance and
          DKIM2-Signature fields by number -- which there are, whether the
          numbers form a chain, how far the signatures reach, each instance
          parsed once. The Verifier, the Signer and the Gate read the chain
          through it (each worked this out for itself); both have a chain()
          accessor.
        - Mail::DKIM2::Hop->next_instance: the Message-Instance a hop adds
          before it signs -- none, m=1, a change from this host's snapshot,
          or one m=1 replacing unsigned instances -- and the message to add
          it to. dkim2-milter, the DKIM2Sign handler and dkim2sign each
          made this decision in their own code.
        - MessageInstance: as_header() and as_header_value(), the field
          folded and ready to insert; changes() and changes_header(), what
          the instance records its hop as changing.
        - Key: signature_algorithm and signature_algorithm_for_key, the one
          table of signing algorithms the Signer and Verifier share.
        - Common.pm is split by subject. Mail::DKIM2::Canon (the fields that
          are not hashed, canonicalization, build_signing_input),
          Mail::DKIM2::Fold (fold_header), Mail::DKIM2::Address (paths,
          domains, the relaxed domain match, the Authentic From check),
          Mail::DKIM2::Key (private keys, key records, Domain Policy
          Records, algorithms) and Mail::DKIM2::RecipeJSON (the r= JSON)
          each hold what their name says; Mail::DKIM2::Util has the two
          helpers they all need. Common keeps the constants, the limits and
          the chain numbering, and still exports every name it ever did:
          "use Mail::DKIM2::Common qw(fold_header)" and
          Mail::DKIM2::Common::relaxed_domain_match(...) work as before.

        The changes of 2026-11-06:

        - Signer: never folds an rt= list at a comma. -09 section 10.6 gives
          rt= no FWS around its commas (a base64string cannot start with
          FWS), though the generic tag-value grammar would allow it; rt=
          still folds inside its base64.
        - An i= or m= is at most two digits now (MAX_CHAIN_NUMBER 99, was
          100 in three digits): with a chain length limit of 32, a third
          digit only ever named a number that is refused anyway. "001" is
          "exceeds the maximum chain number of 99".
        - DSN->authenticate no longer reports ok for a DSN that carries no
          DKIM2-Signature of its own: dsn_result is still none, so a caller
          can relay it as the legacy bounce it is, but anyone holding a
          copy of the returned message could have written it, so
          propagate refuses it rather than re-sign it. (An nd= top
          signature, with no rt= to align with, is unchanged.)
        - Split: plan_copies and disclosed_addresses fold the domain only,
          keeping the local-part's case, so a Bcc to user@ never shares a
          copy (and an rt=) with a To: User@ that may be another mailbox.
        - Security: a header Recipe naming Message-Instance could rewrite
          the instances below it. The undo walk applied it to the received
          fields and checked the lower hashes against what it rebuilt, so a
          hop could replace a message wholesale, swap in an m=1 hashed over
          its own content, and have the chain pass with the original
          reported unchanged. Message-Instance and DKIM2-Signature fields
          are not content (-09 section 6.2): a Recipe naming one acts on
          content fields of that name, of which there are none (copying is
          a Recipe error), as in the other implementations.
        - Verifier: new MailFrom and RcptTo options, the SMTP envelope. Given,
          the top signature must match it (-09 section 14.4): MAIL FROM
          equal to mf=, every RCPT TO in rt=, else fail ("MAIL FROM <x> did
          not match" / "RCPT TO <x> did not match"). The DKIM2Verify
          handler passes both (check_envelope, default on), as does
          dkim2-milter in --mode inbound (--no-envelope-check for an
          internal hop). Before, neither checked, and a message signed for
          one recipient verified when replayed to another.
        - A header field written with white space before its colon
          ("From : x", RFC 5322 obsolete syntax) is a field of that name,
          as -09 section 6.2 has it. Perl kept the white space in the name,
          so such a From was hashed but escaped the From check. New
          Common::field_name and header_values.
        - A header Recipe key must be a header field name (ftext: no white
          space, no colon, -09 section 5), or the Recipe is invalid JSON.
          "message-instance " would otherwise be matched as
          Message-Instance by the name matching above.
          MessageInstance->calculate dies rather than record a change to a
          field whose name is not one (a malformed "Y Bad:" line), which
          no verifier would accept.
        - dkim2-milter: the verdict's detail in Authentication-Results is
          an RFC 5322 comment with its "\", "(" and ")" quoted, printable
          ASCII, at most 200 characters. It quotes signature fields as
          written, so a crafted i= could close the comment and add text
          that read as properties.

0.29    2026-11-03
        draft-ietf-dkim-dkim2-spec-09 and draft-ietf-dkim-dkim2-dns-03.

        0.28. Verification results change as below.

        - A null body Recipe is a PERMERROR: "Message-Instance m=<x> has a
          null recipe", naming the instance that holds it (sections 13,
          14.2). It used to be a pass with fully_verified() false.

          signed. Gate's AllowNullBodyRecipe, dkim2-milter's and

          to refuse it. The gate no longer gives reason

          per domain per message, never prefetched. New Verifier option
          PolicyCallback (and set_policy_callback, fetch_domain_policy);
          without it the lookup goes through Resolver with query(). A
          PubkeyCallback-only caller should add a PolicyCallback, or the
          lookup uses a default resolver. A record beginning v=DKIM1 that
          does not parse counts as f=strict.

          the same policy lookup (Signer options PolicyCallback and
          Resolver, fetch_domain_policy); strict, multiple or unavailable
          refuses, with the reason after "From header field is not
          Authentic for d=...: ". dkim2-milter, dkim2sign and DKIM2Sign
          pass their dns.json or resolver. New Common::from_pair_error,
          query_domain_policy, policy_from_source.
        - New section 14.8 strings: "From <dom> forbids subdomain signing",
          "From has more than one address", "From uses a domain literal",
          "policy for <dom> unavailable" (TEMPERROR), "multiple records
          for <dom> policy" (PERMERROR).
        - Key records: TXT records at the selector that begin with a v=
          other than DKIM1 are ignored before "has multiple records" is
          judged (section 3.7). New Common::key_records, domain_policy,
          from_mailbox.
        - An RSA key under 1024 bits is "public key <s> too short" (was
          "is malformed"); still refused.
        - Strings: "<field> m=/i=<n> is duplicated" (was "appears more than
          once"); "recipe <path> is invalid" (lower case); "mf= and d= do
          not match" (was "MAIL FROM and d="); no DKIM2 header fields at
          all: details "NONE: No DKIM2 header fields found".
        - New check: "PERMERROR: DKIM2-Signature i=1 has an exploded flag",
          before any key is fetched.
        - X-DKIM2-Info: draft=ietf-dkim-dkim2-spec-09 (debug-header-03).
        - Key and policy record parsing trims white space in linear time

0.28    2026-10-28
        draft-ietf-dkim-dkim2-spec-08. Changes what is hashed and what
        verifies, so every signer and verifier must move together:
        Auto-Submitted and VBR-Info are hashed now.

        - Auto-Submitted and VBR-Info are no longer ignored (section 4).
        - h= and s= are "," lists (all must pass) joined by "|" (any may
          pass), and results combine as sections 14.6 and 14.7 say. An
          algorithm this verifier does not implement is a PERMERROR
          item, overridden only by a "|" alternative; an absent key no
          longer just skips its item; the "more selectors than allowed"
          limit is gone. Keys and signatures are checked together, one
          signature at a time. fold_header may fold around "," and "|".
        - Tag-names and JSON keys are case-sensitive and lowercase: an
          uppercase tag is an unknown tag, an uppercase key invalid JSON.
          Hash and algorithm names are case-sensitive too.
        - Timestamp, Chain of Custody and From-Authentic errors are FAIL,
          not PERMERROR (sections 14.3, 14.4, 14.8).
        - New strings: "Recipe <path> is invalid" for one bad Recipe step
          (b[<n>] or h.<name>[<n>]), "public key <s> is malformed" (an
          Ed25519 key not exactly 32 octets, DER included; an RSA key
          under 1024 bits), "selector <s> algorithm unknown", "algorithm
          <name> unknown", "no group of signatures/hashes passed".
          recipe_order_error is gone: parse checks copy-range order.
        - Verifier::fully_verified: false for a pass over a null body
          Recipe, whose lower body hashes cannot be checked (section 13);
          Validate's report carries it.
        - provisionally_verified follows section 13.2: it checks the top
          d= against a non-null top mf=, and no longer the timestamps.
        - DSN->may_generate takes Domain: a DSN's d= must match a
          recipient in the reported message's top rt= (section 16.2).
        - ML-DSA-44 ("mldsa44") is not implemented: algorithm unknown.
        - Local policy, MAX_SIGNATURE_ITEMS: an s= of more than 8 items
          is "has more than 8 signatures", before any key is fetched.
        - Every s= and h= value must be a base64string, whatever its
          algorithm. A Recipe's whole-document faults are reported before
          any step's. provisionally_verified is false under InstancesOnly.
          The validator reads i= and m= case-sensitively. fold_header no
          longer folds between a header hash's padding and its ":".

0.27    2026-10-21
        Fix a test failure on hosts without JSON::XS.

        - A Recipe number with an exponent ({"c":[1e0,3]}) is refused
          whichever JSON backend JSON.pm picks. JSON::PP decodes 1e0 as
          an integer where JSON::XS gives a float, so with JSON::PP 0.25
          and 0.26 accepted it and failed t/recipe-order.t on install.

0.26    2026-10-20
        The Message-Instances are verified before the signatures, and a
        message in a file can be signed and gated without reading it into
        memory. No change to anything on the wire; which error is primary
        changes for messages with more than one fault.

        - New Mail::DKIM2::BodyHasher: the body hash body_digest_raw
          gives, from a message fed through PRINT/CLOSE or load() in
          pieces, holding at most a megabyte of the body. Its
          body_hashes are what calculate's BodyHash and verify's
          BodyHashes take, so a Message-Instance can be computed or
          checked from the header block alone.
        - Verifier order: the Message-Instances are checked first (each
          one's content, then the walk, section 14.7), the signatures
          second (sections 14.2 to 14.6), From last. No key is needed to
          refuse a message whose instances do not describe it, and with
          several faults a hash mismatch is now the primary error over a
          timestamp, custody, key or signature error.
        - Under AllowUnsignedMI or MidProcess, Message-Instances with no
          DKIM2-Signature are walked: 'none' if they match the message,
          the walk's fail or permerror if not (it was 'none' unread).
        - New Verifier option InstancesOnly (instances_only): the chain's
          shape and the Message-Instances, then stop, with no key fetched;
          'pass' ("Message-Instance m=1..N intact") when they match.
        - Gate->check takes a filehandle (or any object with getline) as
          well as a string, and streams its body into the Verifier. The
          chain is walked once, always by the Verifier (InstancesOnly with
          no signature or with VerifyResult); it no longer calls
          MessageInstance->chain_verifies.
        - The Signer discards the body as it arrives (section 12.8 signs
          none of it), and may be fed the header block alone.
        - load() reads a filehandle a piece at a time, and stops reading
          once the parser has stopped (a Verifier with no signature to
          check, after the header fields), instead of reading it whole.

0.25    2026-10-20
        Which error is reported when a message has more than one fault
        (the interop contract's C9, so every implementation names the
        same one), and one verdict.

        - Section 14.2: the chain's structure before any field's content,
          in a fixed order: too many fields; a Message-Instance with no
          usable m=; an m= given twice; a DKIM2-Signature with no usable
          i= (or one out of range); an i= given twice; a missing
          Message-Instance; an instance no signature covers; a missing
          DKIM2-Signature. Then each Message-Instance's content by
          ascending m= (it was highest first), then each signature's.
        - A number given twice is reported by its lowest value, not the
          first met.
        - Section 14.7: within one instance every header hash, in the
          order h= lists the algorithms, before any body hash (it was each
          algorithm in turn, alphabetically).
        - A Message-Instance with no m= is "PERMERROR: Message-Instance
          m= tag=m missing" (was "... without m= tag"); new constant
          Mail::DKIM2::Common::MI_MISSING_M_ERROR.
        - The structure is judged at the end of the header fields, so a
          message whose chain is broken there stops before any key is
          fetched.
        - Verdict change: a message with no DKIM2-Signature and a gap in
          its Message-Instances (only m=2, say) is "PERMERROR: Message-
          Instance m=1 missing" with AllowUnsignedMI or MidProcess too; it
          used to be "none" there. "none" is only for a message with no
          DKIM2 field at all. (The reflector, which uses AllowUnsignedMI,
          no longer bridge-signs such a message.)

0.24    2026-10-19
        Fixes to the public-key prefetch added in 0.22, which made every
        DKIM2-signed message cost about five seconds behind a resolver that
        customises send or query, and one API change.

        - No prefetch through a resolver that subclasses Net::DNS::Resolver
          and overrides send or query (as FastMTA's and authentication_
          milter's do) without its own bgsend: Net::DNS's bgsend bypassed
          that override and asked only the first nameserver, and on a host
          where those background answers never arrived every key waited out
          the deadline before query() asked again. Such a resolver now gets
          every lookup through query(). A plain Net::DNS::Resolver, or one
          with its own bgsend, is prefetched as before.
        - At most $Mail::DKIM2::Verifier::PREFETCH_MAX (8) keys are asked
          for in the background per message, the top signature's first. The
          prefetch runs before any field is judged, and a message naming
          thousands of selectors opened a socket and sent a query for each;
          a key not prefetched is asked for with query() if it is needed.
        - $Mail::DKIM2::Verifier::PREFETCH_WAIT is 1 second (was 5): an
          answer that has not arrived by then is asked again with query().
        - Waiting for a background answer sleeps between polls (5ms,
          $Mail::DKIM2::Verifier::PREFETCH_POLL). Net::DNS's own bgbusy
          already waited briefly, but a resolver whose bgbusy does not block
          made the old loop spin.
        - A truncated background answer (Net::DNS's TCP retry failed) is
          asked again with query() instead of being used.
        - API change: Signer->as_string croaks "no signature: REASON" when
          there is no signature (before CLOSE, or when result is "fail");
          it used to return the empty string, which a caller that
          prepended it without checking result turned into a blank line
          ending the message's header block. Check result first, as every
          caller in this distribution does.

0.23    2026-10-18
        Draft -07 (draft-ietf-dkim-dkim2-spec-07). The wire format and
        many verdicts change: a message 0.22 passed may not pass, and the
        other way round. DKIM2_DRAFT is ietf-dkim-dkim2-spec-07 and
        DKIM2_DATE 2026-10-18. New prerequisite: URI (URI::_punycode).

        Recipes (section 5)
        - A Recipe literal that is valid UTF-8 (ASCII included) is a "d"
          step; one that is not is a "u" step, canonical base64 of the
          octets. The "b" step of 0.13 to 0.22 is gone: on the wire it is
          now an unknown step key, and invalid. MessageInstance->calculate
          emits "u" (the Sympa and Mailman handlers get it from there).
        - Every step has exactly one key, "c", "d" or "u"; bare arrays and
          strings as steps, an empty step, two keys, an unknown key, a "u"
          string that is not canonical base64 (padding, zero pad bits, no
          FWS), a decoded "u" or a "d" holding CR or LF, a "c" that is not
          two integers of at least 1, "h": {}, "h": null, and a Recipe
          object with neither "h" nor "b" are all "PERMERROR:
          Message-Instance m=N contains invalid JSON". So, now, is every
          Recipe that does not undo: a copy range past the end, out of
          order or overlapping.
        - JSON keys are matched without regard to case at every level
          ("H", "Subject", "C" are read as "h", "subject", "c"); two keys
          in one object that differ only in case are a duplicate, invalid
          JSON. Keys are emitted in lower case.
        - Common::decode_tag_json dies on JSON text that is not UTF-8 and
          on a duplicate key in any case, and returns every string, keys
          included, as UTF-8 octets (\u escapes too).
        - A Message-Instance with no r= at m=2 or above is "no change", as
          before; now tested.

        Tag lists (section 8)
        - An empty tag-spec before the end (";;", a leading ";") is a
          syntax error in a Message-Instance and a DKIM2-Signature; one
          trailing ";" is still allowed.
        - A DKIM2-Signature tag repeated in any case is "syntax error" (was
          "duplicate tag X not permitted"). A Message-Instance with no h=
          is "tag=h missing".

        Flags (sections 10.10, 12.5)
        - donotmodify and donotexplode are no longer enforced: f= is a
          list of flags with no verifier meaning.
        - New Signer option Exploded. A signature carries f=exploded when
          i > 1 and Exploded (or "exploded" in Flags) is set, or rt= holds
          more than one address; never at i=1, where a caller-supplied
          "exploded" is dropped. sign_for_recipient works the flag out
          afresh for each recipient set (it builds a new Signature object).
        - dkim2-milter and the DKIM2Sign handler treat an X-DKIM2-Exploded
          header field (any value; Mailman and Sympa add one to each
          distribution copy) as the request, and remove it before signing.
          dkim2sign has --exploded.

        Chain of Custody (sections 7, 14.4)
        - Every signature is checked against the one below it: after an
          nd= hop, d= must be that nd= ("i=P nd= does not match"); an nd=
          hop or one with a null mf= must have its d= at or above a
          previous rt= domain ("i=S d= does not match the rt= of i=P");
          any other its mf= domain at or below one ("i=S mf= does not
          match the rt= of i=P"). A null mf= used to fail outright, and an
          nd= hop's d= was compared the other way round. Every non-null
          mf= must be at or below its own d=, on every signature, not only
          where it was checked before. All are PERMERROR (were "fail").
        - nd= with mf= or rt= is "tag=mf (or rt) was unexpected" (was
          "tag=nd was unexpected"); a missing rt= is "tag=rt missing".
        - New Common::domain_of($addr): the domain of an address or path,
          lowercased, one trailing dot off ("<A@Example.COM.>" is
          example.com), and whether it is a domain literal.
        - New Common::to_alabel($domain): non-ASCII labels as A-labels
          (xn-- Punycode). Signers now record mf= and rt= domains as
          A-labels.
        - Common::relaxed_domain_match compares A-labels, ignores a
          trailing dot, and never matches a domain literal; only its first
          argument is shortened, as before.

        From must be Authentic (sections 11, 12.4, 14.8)
        - The Verifier checks the From in effect when each signature was
          made: the From at state m(i=1) against i=1, and, for each i >= 2
          where an instance in (m(i-1), m(i)] changed From, the From at
          state m(i) against i: exactly one From field, one mailbox, its
          domain (as A-labels, never a literal) at or below d=. Otherwise
          "PERMERROR: DKIM2-Signature i=N matching From is not authentic".
          A From replaced before any signature covered it (an unsigned
          ingress m=1 a list rewrote in m=2 before signing i=1) is never
          checked. Instances no signature covers (AllowUnsignedMI, the
          signer gate) are not checked: the Signer checks those.
        - The Signer refuses (result fail, details "From header field is
          not Authentic for d=D") when the message has no DKIM2-Signature
          yet, or a Message-Instance no signature covers names From, and
          the From is not Authentic for its Domain.
        - New Common::from_domain(@values) and Common::from_authentic($d,
          @values); new HeaderPlan::values_at($m, $name).
        - DSN->generate and DSN->propagate sign From
          "Mail Delivery System <postmaster@" the signer's Domain ">".
        - An unsigned post on the stock-Mailman route (and any message
          whose Message-Instances no DKIM2-Signature covers) leaves
          dkim2-milter and the DKIM2Sign handler with ONE m=1, as -07
          section 12.1 allows: hashes of the copy sent and Recipes back to
          the post as it arrived, a From munge included (so C5 checks the
          munged From against i=1). The instances it carried are removed
          and X-DKIM2-Info records action=restarted-unsigned-mi=m=1,...;
          the message as it arrived comes from those instances when the top
          one matches, else from the X-DKIM2-Snapshot snapshot. A post that
          arrived signed is extended as before (m=N+1).
        - MessageInstance->calculate($msg, $previous) with no instances on
          either gives m=1 with Recipes (it died before). New
          MessageInstance->calculate_first($msg, $previous): the m=1 above,
          undoing every instance of $previous.

        Error strings and results (section 14)
        - details() is the -07 human-readable string, state included:
          "STATE: text", e.g. "PERMERROR: Message-Instance m=2 missing",
          "FAIL: Message-Instance m=1 body hash sha256 mismatch". Checks
          with no -07 string keep their words with a "PERMERROR: " prefix,
          including Common's chain_length_error, chain_number_error (a
          malformed number is now "Field tag=X syntax error"),
          duplicate_number_error and UNKEYABLE_SIGNATURE_ERROR, and
          Signature::check_duplicates. For pass and none, details() is
          unchanged.
        - Now permerror, were fail: a missing DKIM2-Signature or
          Message-Instance (also one a signature covers that is not
          there), every Chain of Custody failure, a timestamp out of range,
          an unbracketed mf= or rt= ("syntax error"), no algorithm this
          verifier implements, a Recipe that does not undo.
        - Every signature item that can be checked is checked: all failing
          is "FAIL: DKIM2-Signature i=N selector S incorrect signature",
          some passing and some failing "FAIL: DKIM2-Signature i=N
          signature S1 signature S2 failed" (one failing used to end the
          check).
        - "TEMPERROR: DKIM2-Signature i=N public key S could not be
          fetched" loses its "(why)" suffix: the resolver's reason, and the
          range behind a Recipe that does not undo, are in the new
          Verifier::diagnostic().
        - Every Message-Instance is parsed (syntax, h=, Recipe JSON) before
          any signature is worked out, so a malformed one is reported as
          such rather than as the signature it breaks.
        - MessageInstance->verify and ->chain_verifies give the same
          strings; chain_verifies gives the reason a Recipe did not undo as
          a third value.

        Timestamps (section 14.3)
        - A t= more than a day ahead is "PERMERROR: DKIM2-Signature i=N
          signature is from the future" (was five minutes, and fail); more
          than 14 days old "signature expired" (was fail). New Common
          constants FUTURE_LIMIT (86400) and EXPIRY (1209600).

        DSNs and SMTP (sections 13, 16)
        - New Verifier::provisionally_verified (section 13.1): the top
          signature is correct and the top Message-Instance matches,
          whatever else failed.
        - New DSN->may_generate: never a DSN when the top mf= is <> or the
          message is not Provisionally Verified. DSN->generate croaks
          unless it may (new options PubkeyCallback, Resolver,
          SkipTimestampCheck), and no longer falls back to the From header
          field for the destination. DSN->propagate croaks rather than
          send towards a null mf=.
        - Reflector::generate_dsn and dkim2-reflector.pl send a DSN only
          for a Provisionally Verified message, and log why not.
        - dkim2-milter and the DKIM2Sign handler reject with 550 5.7.1 and
          the reason (smfi_setreply, reject_mail) a message carrying an
          upstream DKIM2-Signature that the gate or the Signer refuses to
          sign; such a message used to be sent on unsigned. One with no
          signature still goes on unsigned, this host's instances removed.

        Reflector (section 11)

          changes it (any mode but raw), From becomes "<sender's name or
          address> via DKIM2 reflector" <reflector-<mode>@<domain>>, the
          sender's From kept as Reply-To if there is none. Originating
          without a DKIM2-Signature to continue drops the inbound
          Message-Instance and starts again at m=1.

        Validate.pm reports Chain of Custody by the -07 rules and the same
        strings, and grades a timestamp over a day ahead as "future".

        Error strings for i= and m= numbers, as all five interop verifiers
        now give them: a DKIM2-Signature with no i= is "PERMERROR:
        DKIM2-Signature i= tag=i missing" (UNKEYABLE_SIGNATURE_ERROR, was
        "has a missing or malformed i= tag"), one whose i= is not a
        positive integer "i=<as written> syntax error" (new
        Common::unkeyable_signature_error); a signature's malformed m= is
        "DKIM2-Signature i=<i> syntax error"; an out-of-range number names
        the field and the value ("DKIM2-Signature i=33 exceeds the maximum
        chain length of 32", "DKIM2-Signature i=2 m=101 exceeds ...",
        "Message-Instance m=101 exceeds ..."). Common::chain_number_error
        takes the field's own number as a fourth argument.

        Check order and the primary result (interop contract C9)

          go through the new Mail::DKIM2::Digest: OpenSSL's SHA-2, through
          Net::SSLeay, when that is installed (recommended, not required),
          else CryptX's as before. The digests are the same; OpenSSL uses
          the CPU's SHA instructions where there are some -- about 7 times
          CryptX's speed on an Apple M-series, 1.8 times on an older x86.
        - The body is hashed where it lies, in whole runs, with fewer
          copies: load() normalises line endings only when there is a bare
          LF and never changes the caller's string; PRINT hands body chunks
          straight to the Verifier's body plan.
        - The Verifier checks the Message-Instance chain without rebuilding
          any previous version of the message. New: Mail::DKIM2::BodyPlan
          composes the body Recipes into, for each instance, the runs of
          current body lines and Recipe literals its body was, and hashes
          every instance's body in one pass as the body arrives; the body is
          not kept. New: Mail::DKIM2::HeaderPlan does the same for header
          fields, canonicalizing each hashed value once. Same verdicts, in
          the same words; about 40% less time on list mail, all of it in
          the chain check. Verifier option StreamBody (on by default); 0 is
          the undo walk.

          from it (a snapshot, or a first Message-Instance).

          in the background (Net::DNS bgsend), as soon as it has the header
          fields, and reads the answers when it checks the signatures; an

          asked again with query(). Each key name is looked up once per
          message. A chain of five signing domains verified about four times
          faster against live DNS.

          headers, then each body chunk), so the key lookups overlap the
          body's transfer.

          Message-Instance to mail it does not sign (no key for the sender,
          a refused chain, a signer failure), and removes every
          Message-Instance no DKIM2-Signature covers -- instances hops on
          this host added for a signature that is not going to be made --
          recording it as X-DKIM2-Info: action=removed-unsigned-mi=...;.

          which receivers report as permerror ("m=N is not signed"). An
          unsigned post now leaves with no DKIM2 at all, and a signed one
          fails honestly against the sender's signature. DKIM2Sign does the
          same on a refusal, a domain with no signing configuration, or a
          Signer failure.

          Message-Instance (the diff against the snapshot) before checking
          the upstream chain, and checks the message as it will be signed.
          It used to check first, so a list manager that changed a message
          without recording an instance of its own -- every list copy
          whose changes only the snapshot diff records -- was refused.

          Message-Instance value. A post that replayed a sender's genuine
          m=1 over an edited body found the genuine post's snapshot, and
          the edit was recorded and signed as this host's own change. The
          inbound milter now snapshots only a message it stamps m=1 or
          whose top instance matches the content, stores the snapshot under
          a random token and names it in a new X-DKIM2-Snapshot header; the
          outbound milter diffs only against the snapshot that token names.

          token neither comes from outside nor leaves the host. The inbound
          and outbound milters must share --snapshot-dir (as before) and be
          upgraded together. The authentication_milter handlers do the same:

        Fixes from an external review against spec-06. Several are
        behaviour changes for messages that are malformed or adversarial;
        well-formed mail verifies as before.
        - Behaviour change: only the signature algorithms rsa-sha256 and
          ed25519-sha256, matched exactly, are verified. An s= item naming
          anything else is ignored before its key is fetched (spec-06 §3.4);
          it used to be fetched and verified as RSA, so a correctly
          RSA-signed item declaring an unknown algorithm passed, and many
          distinct unknown names meant as many sequential DNS lookups. s= is
          parsed once, not once per item accessed. A signature whose items
          all name unknown algorithms is FAIL "has no signature with a
          supported algorithm"; a known item whose value is not a padded
          base64string is PERMERROR "syntax error"; a key of the wrong type
          for the algorithm is PERMERROR "algorithm mismatch".
        - Behaviour change: key records are validated whole
          (Mail::DKIM2::Common::parse_dkim_key_record, new): a repeated tag,
          v= not first or not exactly DKIM1, a missing, unpadded or
          non-base64 p=, or a p= that is not a key make the record a syntax
          error; an empty p= is revoked; k= other than rsa or ed25519 is no
          longer read as RSA. More than one TXT record for a selector is an
          error (one record in several strings is joined). The verifier
          reports these as spec-06 §11.5's PERMERRORs naming the selector, and
          a key absent for every item as PERMERROR "public key <sel> does not
          exist". parse_dkim_pubkey keeps its key-or-undef contract.
        - Behaviour change: Message-Instance tag names are case insignificant
          (spec-06 §7): M= and H= are read as m= and h= everywhere, and a tag
          repeated in any case is PERMERROR "syntax error" -- a wrong h= ahead
          of the right one used to be overwritten and pass.
        - Behaviour change: t= must be 1*DIGIT; anything else is PERMERROR
          "syntax error", even with SkipTimestampCheck, and t=0 is subject to
          the age check.
        - Behaviour change: a failed signature item reads "DKIM2-Signature
          i=N <selector> incorrect signature" (spec-06 §11.6).

          algorithm as this repository's C, Python, Go and Mailman
          generators (vectors/body-diff.json); Algorithm::Diff is no longer a
          prerequisite. Repeated-line bodies no longer take quadratic time.

          calculate option, default 1000); over that the default path gives
          the null body Recipe, and EpilogueThreshold (no longer capped) the
          epilogue. dkim2-milter --max-recipe-literals and the DKIM2Sign
          handler's max_recipe_literals set it. An unchanged body under
          EpilogueThreshold gets no Recipe instead of an epilogue copy.

          takes named options croaks on one it does not know, as the
          CONVENTIONS always said (Signature->new, MessageInstance
          calculate/verify/undo/chain_verifies, Gate->check, DSN
          generate/authenticate/propagate, MessageStore->new,

        (interop util/charset-corpus.sh).

          {"b": [base64, ...]} step instead of {"d": [...]}. A literal is
          the raw octets of a header value or body line; JSON text is
          UTF-8, so the old encoder wrote ISO-2022-JP, GB18030, Big5 and

          RFC 4648 base64 or decodes to something containing CR or LF.
          Agreed extension to spec-06 §5, proposed to the WG.
          (t/recipe-base64.t)
        - Recipe copy ranges must ascend (spec-06 §5.1): each "c" step
          starts after the one before it ends. undo() used to sort the
          ranges and reject only overlap; it now rejects an out-of-order
          range too, for body and header Recipes alike. The header Recipe
          builder in calculate() no longer emits one: a header instance a
          hop moved above one it left alone is recorded literally.
          (t/recipe-order.t, t/undo-bounds.t)
        - Two more Recipe schema rules the other verifiers already hold, so
          every implementation gives the same verdict: a "c" bound must be
          a JSON integer (a string such as "2" is malformed; told apart by
          the scalar's flags, not its text), an empty "d" or "b" array is
          malformed (minItems 1), and so is a "d" string containing CR or
          LF (§5.1/§5.2 MUST NOT). (t/recipe-order.t, t/recipe-base64.t)
        - Recipe copy ranges are emitted as JSON integers. An index used as
          a hash key while de-duplicating header copies was stringified in
          place, so every Sympa Message-Instance carried {"c":["2","2"]},
          which the spec-06 schema forbids and strict verifiers reject.
          (t/recipe-integers.t)
        - A broken Content-Type (`text/plain; Windows-1252`) no longer makes
          every verification print Email::MIME's "Illegal parameter" warning:
          the library parses with parameter checking relaxed, for the parse
          only, since DKIM2 never reads a MIME parameter.
          (t/malformed-content-type.t)
        - The test suite is self-contained: the test keys and dns.json ship
          under t/data/ (t/data-in-sync.t keeps them equal to the interop
          repository's shared copies), bin/validate.pl takes --dns-json and
          defaults to that copy, and the tests that cross-check the other
          implementations or the deployment templates skip outside the
          repository. 0.10's tests could not run from the tarball.

          MidProcess, HeadersOnly, PubkeyCallback, Resolver, IgnorePrefixes)

          verifier as a third argument.

      0:0:0:0:0:0:0:7F/8. A negative number gives undef. The
      constructors new6FFFF() and new_cis6() use this same reading, so
      new6FFFF('5', 8) is 0:0:0:0:0:FFFF:0:5/8 where it was
      0:0:0:0:0:FFFF:500:0/104, and a negative number is undef from
      both. An IPv4 reading still gains the mapped prefix. An IPv6
      address stays as new6 gives it.

    - Fix GH#236: An IPv4 address with a mask written as a whole number
      wider than 32 bits needs the 96 leading ones, as the same mask in
      IPv6 form already did. So new('192.0.2.4', N), with N the number
      for ffff::, gives undef where it gave 192.0.2.4/0.

    - Fix GH#235: A small number given with a mask written as a whole
      number, as numeric() returns it, is read as the address value. So
      new(5, 4294967292) gives 0.0.0.5/30 where it gave 5.0.0.0/30. A
      numeric mask of 0 is still prefix length 0, so 0.0.0.5/0 comes
      back as 5.0.0.0/0 and ::1/0 comes back as ::100:0/96. With a
      prefix length the number is still the first octet: new('10', 8)
      is 10.0.0.0/8.

      It wrote ffff into every address, so 2001:db8::1 came back as
      2001:db8::ffff:0:1 and ::1 as ::ffff:0:1. An IPv6 address,
      including ::192.0.2.1 and a keyword such as loopback, now comes
      back as new6 gives it.

      $ip->compactref(), gives the object's network, as $ip->compact()
      does, where it gave blocks built from the host addresses inside it,

      each address once. A subnet listed twice, or a subnet inside

      NetAddr::IP::Lite, or giving either to within() or contains(),

      no longer dies. The operators <=>, <, >, <= and >= give undef or

      eq does.

      undef unless it covers exactly one subnet, as the POD says and as

      gives undef where it gave 192.0.2.5/30, a network that also holds

      does. The tag makes Storable freeze objects as a plain hash. Reading
      data frozen that way does not need it. Importing the tag stops a
      CIDR-string freeze from thawing in the program, or in the calling
      thread under ithreads.

      the keyword's IPv6 address. That covers a separate mask, a mask
      written in the string and an undef mask. The calls

      0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1/64, and new6('loopback', undef) gives
      0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1/128. A separate mask used to keep the keyword's
      own prefix, and a mask in the string or an undef mask used the
      IPv4 keyword. A mask that is not valid gives undef.

      stay hex, as do short(), addr() and stringification, so canon()
      and short() no longer agree on a mapped address, and re() and
      re6() do not match its canon() form. This changes canon()

      after a dot, such as 2001:db8::1.443, do not match either.

      in every group with a subnet that contains it, where 2.01 counted it in

      or IPv4-compatible address and an IPv4 answer exists. A short

      still go to gethostbyname. A name whose only answer is an IPv6
      address in ::/96, such as ip6-localhost at ::1, now gives that

      whole string as the address in the InetBase and Util text functions.
      A part such as the 010 in 192.0.2.010 is octal 8 to the C library's
      inet_aton and decimal 10 to a person. Through gethostbyname, inet_aton
      and new() read it as octal, while ipv6_aton and inet_any2n read it as
      decimal, so the same text named two addresses. Such text is now not an
      address anywhere except new_no(), which reads it as decimal as before.
      The patterns of fillIPv4 and of the dotted quad tail in ipv6_aton
      ended in $, which matches before a final newline, so one trailing
      newline was ignored on some forms and not others. They now end in \z,
      and inet_aton and naip_gethostbyname return undef for text with
      whitespace without asking the resolver. The constructors keep
      stripping surrounding whitespace from the address, as they have since
      4.080_01 (GH#5), now strip it from a separate mask as well, and under
      :aton keep the ends only of a string of four or sixteen bytes. A
      prefix length keeps its leading zeros, so 192.0.2.0/024 is still
      192.0.2.0/24. Against 4.079 these change:
      call                              4.079              now
      inet_aton("192.0.2.1\n")          192.0.2.1          undef
      inet_aton("192.0.2.010")          192.0.2.8          undef
      ipv6_aton("::ffff:192.0.2.1\n")   ::ffff:192.0.2.1   undef
      inet_any2n("192.0.2.010")         ::192.0.2.10       undef
      new("010")                        0.0.0.10/32        undef
      new("192.0.2.010")                192.0.2.8/32       undef
      new("::ffff:192.0.2.010")         ::ffff:192.0.2.10  undef
      new("192.0.2.0", "24\n")          undef              192.0.2.0/24

    - Fix GH#101: Remove the autoconf/configure step. The XS build ran one of
      two autoconf scripts to write xs/config.h, and the C code takes exactly
      two facts from that file: the host byte order and a pair of 32-bit
      integer types. Both have been in perl.h since at least 5.005_03. The
      configure step can go: four files, 31 percent of the compressed tarball,
      about 60 lines of the Makefile.PL header, and the reason the module has
      historically given for building pure Perl on Windows.

    - Fix GH#102: Four helpers in xs/Util.xs read the caller's packed address
      as 32-bit words through a cast of the Perl string buffer. That is
      undefined behaviour in C whenever the buffer is not 4-byte aligned, and
      Perl hands the XSUBs unaligned buffers in ordinary use. A string whose
      leading bytes were removed in place keeps its allocation and moves its
      start. On x86 and arm64 the loads still give the right answer, which is
      why nothing has failed; on hardware that traps misaligned loads, SPARC
      above all, the process dies with SIGBUS. The fix copies the bytes into
      local words with memcpy, which compiles to the same instructions where
      unaligned loads are cheap.

    - Fix GH#7: Document that uppercase is the effective default, not
      lowercase. InetBase said "This module defaults to lowercase", which
      holds only when it is loaded on its own. NetAddr::IP::Util loads it with
      :upper, so every program that uses NetAddr::IP prints uppercase. The
      case setting is process wide and the last import or call wins, so a
      lower() anywhere changes what every object prints. InetBase, IP.pm and
      Lite.pm now say so.

      whether the input was a packed binary address, so bytes 0x41-0x5A (A-Z)
      became 0x61-0x7a (a-z). Fixed by preserving the original input in $raw
      before lowercasing, and using it for the binary IP detection path.

    - comparisons of the form <, >, <=, >=

      return now return the comparison of the cidr value when the address
      portion is equal.
    - NOTE: this comparison returns the comparison of the NUMERIC value of the
      CIDR. This produces the counter intuitive result that /24 > /16. There
      is logic to this, really! For proper operation of commands like
      "Compact" and "Coalesce", lists of netaddr objects must sort in
      ascending order. However, this conflicts with the requirement for larger
      netblocks to sort FIRST so as to include smaller ones. This logic
      extends to any requirement for a sort of netaddr objects. It should be
      further noted that the mixing of netaddr objects with varying IP
      addresses and CIDR allocations can lead to unexpected results since the
      comparisons done first on the IP portion and then on the CIDR portion.
      The documentation has been updated appropriately.

v0.3.6 2026-11-17

    A pipeline can be fed its values as they arrive, from a library
    that calls you back, an event loop, or a stage running its values
    through a pipeline of its own; and tee, built on that, is a tap of
    any shape, running each value through a branch of stages beside
    the main run.

    It ships roadmap 2026-0044 and 2026-0048. It only adds: pushed and
    pulled runs, the messages, and the order things run in are as they
    were, and no slower; a push through plain stages is a little faster.

    - $pipeline->feed returns an Ekorn::Pipeline::Feed, one run, made
      then: push runs values through the stages, and returns what came
      out of them; close ends the input, and returns what the flushes
      give, and a sink's result; finish ends the run as from outside;
      ended says how it ended. Fed the same values, a feed gives what
      a call gives, a push at a time. A stop ends the run in the push
      that meets it. Once the run has ended, a push or a close croaks,
      "Expected a feed still open, but its run has ended", so values
      can't go nowhere unnoticed; a push, close or finish from inside
      the feed's own run croaks too. A feed has no context of its own:
      its stages see the context of the code pushing into it, none from
      outside a run. A push costs about 1.3 µs a value through a bare
      stage, and 2 µs through a gather with a flush, on Perl 5.36 and
      5.44. The user guide shows a library's callbacks feeding a
      function's caller's stages, a tee running values through a
      branch of stages beside the main run, and a stage running each
      key's values through a run of their own. (roadmap 2026-0044)
    - tee(@stages), in Ekorn::Pipeline::Stages::Taps, exported on
      request and in :all and Ekorn::Pipeline::Tooling's :taps, runs
      each value through a branch of the stages, and passes it on
      unchanged; what comes out of the branch is dropped. The branch is
      one run of its own, beside the main run, fed by a feed made for
      each main run, so its stages keep their state across the values.
      A stop in it, such as take's, ends only the branch. A death in it
      kills the run, named as the tee's stage, then the branch's within
      it. Its flushes are called in the tee's flush, and its ends as its
      run ends, or, if the main run ended first, in the tee's end, told
      stopped. The branch sees the main run's context, so stages that
      read it, such as a statement's columns, work there. It takes
      whatever new takes, a pipeline or a sink last included. A tee has
      a flush and an end only if its branch needs them, so a branch of
      plain stages leaves the main run on the plain loop, and costs
      about 1.3 µs a value, against peek's 0.4. (roadmap 2026-0048)
    - A push through plain stages, and through stages made with gather
      that have no flush or end, copies its values once less, costing
      about 5% less a value: through one plain stage, 332 to 335 ns,
      not 348 to 360, on Perl 5.36, and 370 to 375, not 395 to 411, on
      5.44.

    doesn't leak a password, a token or a DSN.

    Text::Redact::Secrets is installed: then dumps are redacted, and
    a module that's there but broken makes dump_to croak, with a new

    - dump_to redacts with Text::Redact::Secrets' redact when it's
      installed, a v1.x, and passes a self-test, redacting a few
      made-up secrets in a dump: each secret it finds in what's
      written, such as a password, a token or the password in a DSN,
      is written as *REDACTED*. Only the dump is redacted: the value
      passed on is as it came. The module is looked for once, at the

    told how it ended, with words to make them and | to join them.

    Pipelines can be made with pipeline(), and named, and a function
    whose values can be code references can take its stages as a
    pipeline given last. pipeline() is one of the words in
    Ekorn::Pipeline::Factories, short functions that make Ekorn's
    types: stage, gather, source, generator with yield, sink_one and
    sink_many. The README's CPAN badge keeps up with releases, and the
    how-to says where a stage belongs. Stages::Flow has take_first,
    take_last and take_single, and take_if and drop_if, which filter.
    Ekorn::Pipeline::Tooling exports every stage, source, sink and
    word from one module, by tags. Ekorn::Pipeline::JSON reads and
    writes JSON and JSON Lines, as sources, stages or sinks, and
    Ekorn::Pipeline::Sugar names pipelines as the program compiles,
    each with a function of its name.

    A run's parts can be made afresh for it, and told how it ended:
    sources that close what they open, however the run ends; sinks
    that consume every value and give a result, committing only when
    the run is done; and gathers with an end as well as a flush, what
    v0.2.0 called the end function; Sources and Sinks have them
    ready-made, and Operators joins them with |. A part's set-up, or
    a package's role method, can return its parts by name, as a hash
    reference, rather than as a list in a set order. An iterator is an
    object, which can read what's left in one call, end its run early,
    and say how it ended, and which ends its run when it's let go.

    Pushing values through plain subs is several times faster, reading
    an iterator's values in one call a tenth faster, and a stop about
    three times cheaper.

    It ships nineteen roadmap items, 2026-0009, 2026-0010, 2026-0011,
    2026-0013, 2026-0014, 2026-0016, 2026-0017, 2026-0018, 2026-0021,
    2026-0024, 2026-0025, 2026-0026, 2026-0027, 2026-0028, 2026-0029,
    2026-0030, 2026-0031, 2026-0032 and 2026-0034. It changes what
    some code sees, as the entries marked "Changed" say: a gather, an
    iterator, every canned stage, and the stages a pipeline gives back
    are objects, called as code references, not code references
    themselves; a gather's message names the flush and the end; a
    stage's error names the named pipeline it's in; the messages for
    what isn't a stage or a source say what one is; and a pipeline
    named alone, pipeline('clean'), is the pipeline itself, so its
    stages are numbered where it's given. Otherwise, existing code
    runs as before.

      array of pairs, names each in the package that uses it, and gives
      that package a function of each name, which runs values through
      the pipeline, and, given a pipeline last, through that too. A
      definition can name any other in the same use, in either order.
      Mistakes, such as a name taken already, or a circle of names,
      croak as the use compiles. import_into does the same for a
      package given, for other modules' sugar. Sub::Util, which comes
      with Perl, is a new dependency. (roadmap 2026-0010)

    A pipeline can be fed its values as they arrive, from a library
    that calls you back, an event loop, or a stage running its values
    through a pipeline of its own; and tee, built on that, is a tap of
    any shape, running each value through a branch of stages beside
    the main run.

    It ships roadmap 2026-0044 and 2026-0048. It only adds: pushed and
    pulled runs, the messages, and the order things run in are as they
    were, and no slower; a push through plain stages is a little faster.

    - $pipeline->feed returns an Ekorn::Pipeline::Feed, one run, made
      then: push runs values through the stages, and returns what came
      out of them; close ends the input, and returns what the flushes
      give, and a sink's result; finish ends the run as from outside;
      ended says how it ended. Fed the same values, a feed gives what
      a call gives, a push at a time. A stop ends the run in the push
      that meets it. Once the run has ended, a push or a close croaks,
      "Expected a feed still open, but its run has ended", so values
      can't go nowhere unnoticed; a push, close or finish from inside
      the feed's own run croaks too. A feed has no context of its own:
      its stages see the context of the code pushing into it, none from
      outside a run. A push costs about 1.3 µs a value through a bare
      stage, and 2 µs through a gather with a flush, on Perl 5.36 and
      5.44. The user guide shows a library's callbacks feeding a
      function's caller's stages, a tee running values through a
      branch of stages beside the main run, and a stage running each
      key's values through a run of their own. (roadmap 2026-0044)
    - tee(@stages), in Ekorn::Pipeline::Stages::Taps, exported on
      request and in :all and Ekorn::Pipeline::Tooling's :taps, runs
      each value through a branch of the stages, and passes it on
      unchanged; what comes out of the branch is dropped. The branch is
      one run of its own, beside the main run, fed by a feed made for
      each main run, so its stages keep their state across the values.
      A stop in it, such as take's, ends only the branch. A death in it
      kills the run, named as the tee's stage, then the branch's within
      it. Its flushes are called in the tee's flush, and its ends as its
      run ends, or, if the main run ended first, in the tee's end, told
      stopped. The branch sees the main run's context, so stages that
      read it, such as a statement's columns, work there. It takes
      whatever new takes, a pipeline or a sink last included. A tee has
      a flush and an end only if its branch needs them, so a branch of
      plain stages leaves the main run on the plain loop, and costs
      about 1.3 µs a value, against peek's 0.4. (roadmap 2026-0048)
