 [`read_table`]

 - Bug fixes:

 - **A comment-prefixed header is now read correctly.** `read_table` strips a
     leading comment marker from the header line (so a file may begin with
     `#id,val`), but that strip was dead code: the XS parser skipped *every* line
     beginning with the comment string before the callback ever saw it, so a
     commented header was silently dropped and the first data row was mistaken for
     the header. The parser now delivers the first content line even when it
     begins with the comment marker, and only skips comment lines after the header
     has been seen.

 - **Carriage returns inside quoted fields are preserved.** The parser stripped
     `\r` unconditionally, so a quoted value such as `"x\ry"` lost its carriage
     return and would not survive a `write_table` -> `read_table` round-trip. `\r`
     is now stripped only as part of a trailing CRLF line ending and as a stray CR
     *outside* quotes; inside quotes it is literal data.

 - **Duplicate column names no longer corrupt `hoa` output.** With
     `output.type => 'hoa'`, a repeated column name pushed the same cell once per
     occurrence, so the affected columns came out longer than the others and the
     arrays no longer lined up by row. Columns are now keyed by unique header name
     (first-seen order preserved, later values win, one warning emitted).

 - **A defined non-CODE callback is now an error.** Passing a defined argument
     that was not a CODE reference silently fell through to slurp mode and ignored
     the argument; it now croaks
     (*"callback must be a CODE reference"*).

 - **An undefined/empty `hoh` row-name now dies instead of keying on `""`.**
     With `output.type => 'hoh'`, a row whose row-name column was empty/undef was
     stored under the `''` key and raised *"uninitialized value"* warnings. It now
     dies, naming the column and the offending data row.

 - **A numeric filter key past the last column now dies.** A 1-based numeric
     filter key greater than the column count was accepted, then silently extended
     every row through the `$_` write-back. It is now rejected up front with a
     message naming the column count.

 - **`sep` and `delim` together now die.** Supplying both silently preferred
     `delim`; passing both is now an explicit error (`delim` remains an alias for
     `sep` when used alone).

 - **The library no longer prints to STDOUT.** The unknown-argument path used
     `say` to dump the offending names to STDOUT before dying; the names are now
     carried in the `die` message itself.

 - Better diagnostics:

 - Alignment errors now report **which data row** is ragged
     (*"Alignment error on FILE data row N (X fields vs Y headers)"*), instead of
     only the field/header counts.

 - Memory-leak fixes (exception paths):

 - The parser allocated its working buffers (`current_row`, `field`, and — in
   slurp mode — `data`) in the XS `INIT:` block, i.e. *before* any validation, and
   freed them only by falling off the end of the function. Any non-local exit
   therefore leaked:

 - the open-failure `croak` leaked the row buffer and field (and the slurp
     accumulator);
 - far more commonly, a `die` thrown **inside the row callback** — which
     `read_table` does routinely on alignment errors, bad row names, and filter
     exceptions — unwound straight out of the XS frame and leaked the field, the
     current row, the line buffer, the slurp accumulator, *and the open file
     handle*.

 - Allocations now happen in `CODE:` after every croak-able check, and every
   long-lived resource (the file handle via `SAVEDESTRUCTOR_X`, the buffers via
   `SAVEFREESV`) is tied to the save stack, which an exception unwinds. Measured
   with `Test::LeakTrace`: a `die` mid-file went from 5 leaked SVs to 0, and an
   open failure from 2 to 0. This is the likely source of the constant-size leaks
   seen in CPAN-tester reports for the exception-path tests.

 - Performance:

 - **~2.5x faster parsing** (57 -> 145 MB/s on a 100k-row quoted file). The core
     loop appended one character at a time with `sv_catpvn(field, &ch, 1)`; it now
     scans runs of ordinary bytes with `memchr` / a bounded scan and appends each
     run in a single `sv_catpvn`, copying field contents in bulk rather than byte
     by byte.

 - Internal / non-behavioral:

 - XS declarations moved from `INIT:` to `PREINIT:`; allocations deferred into
     `CODE:` (see the leak fixes above).
 - The filter loop now aliases the row hash with `local *_ = \%line_hash`
     instead of copying it with `local %_ = %line_hash`. This removes a full
     per-row hash copy for every filtered row and fixes a latent staleness bug:
     after a filter mutated `$_` and the change was written back, `%_` still
     reflected the pre-mutation copy, so a subsequent filter in the same row saw
     stale values. With aliasing, `%_` *is* the row, so write-backs are always
     visible.

 - Known limitation (not changed):

 - **`undef.val` does not round-trip back to `undef`.** `write_table` renders an
     `undef` cell as an empty field by default, and `read_table` maps an empty
     field back to `undef`, so the *default* round-trip is clean. But if a file is
     written with a token such as `'undef.val' => 'NA'`, `read_table` has no
     inverse option and reads `NA` back as the string `'NA'`. `read_table` also
     cannot distinguish a deliberately quoted empty string (`""`) from a missing
     value -- both become `undef`. Adding an `na.strings`-style option to
     `read_table` (mapping configurable tokens and/or empty fields to `undef`)
     would close this gap.

 [`write_table`]

 - Behavior change:

 - **`undef` cells now write as an empty field, not an empty string.** A missing
     or `undef` value renders as nothing between separators (`a,,c`) rather than a
     quoted empty string (`a,'',c` / `a,"",c`). Supplying `'undef.val' => 'NA'`
     (or any other token) still overrides this, exactly as before. This is the
     only change that can alter the bytes of an existing output file; if you relied
     on the previous default, pass `'undef.val' => ''` to keep an explicit empty
     field, or your chosen placeholder.

 - Bug fixes:

 - **Wide-character / UTF-8 column names and row keys now round-trip.**
     Previously, cells were looked up with the raw bytes of the column name
     (`hv_fetch(..., SvPV_nolen(name), strlen(name), ...)`), which fails to match a
     UTF-8-flagged hash key: the column header printed correctly but every cell
     under it came back empty. All lookups now fetch by SV (`hv_fetch_ent`), header
     lists are gathered and sorted as SVs (`sortsv` + `sv_cmp`, preserving the
     flag) instead of being round-tripped through `char *`, and the `row.names`
     column is matched with `sv_eq` rather than `strcmp`. Embedded NUL bytes in
     keys are handled correctly as a side effect.

 - **`col.names => []` no longer loops forever.** An empty `col.names` array made
     `av_len()` return `-1`, which — compared against an unsigned `size_t` loop
     index — wrapped to `SIZE_MAX` and ran effectively without end. This was fixed
     for flat hashes previously; it was still present for hash-of-hashes,
     hash-of-arrays, and array-of-hashes, plus both `row.names` header-filtering
     loops. All such loops now use a signed index.

 - **Tables wider than 65,535 columns no longer hang.** One header loop used an
     `unsigned short` index that silently wrapped past 65,535 and never terminated.
     It now uses `size_t` like the rest of the code.

 - **Flat-hash cells holding a reference now croak.** Every other input shape
     rejects a nested reference with
     *"Cannot write nested reference types to table"*; a flat hash instead
     stringified it (e.g. `ARRAY(0x55...)`) into the file. It now croaks
     consistently.

 - **`'undef.val' => undef` is handled cleanly.** It previously called
     `SvPV_nolen` on `undef`, raising an *"uninitialized value"* warning and
     yielding an empty string by accident. It is now treated explicitly as an empty
     field, with no warning.

 - The row-key list gathered for hash-of-hashes input was leaked when the output
     file could not be opened.
 - The *"Could not get headers"* croak on hash-of-arrays input leaked both the
     already-open filehandle and the headers array.

     cast-away-`const` and one allocation per row).

     `size_t`) to match `av_len()` and silence the conditions behind the loop bugs

     empty input writing no file, and UTF-8 column names and row keys. Two leak

v0.0.59 2026-11-27T11:08:42Z

    - INCOMPATIBLE: the protocol version is now 2, so this release needs
      clients of this release, and its clients need a server of it.
      Upgrade both together
    - Changes at the ends of an array in a channel's state are now sent as
      small diffs: items removed from the start or the end and items added
      at the start, as well as items added at the end as before. That
      covers push, pop, shift and unshift, alone or together. Previously
      everything but a push sent the whole array

v0.0.58 2026-11-26T13:50:09Z

    - A graceful stop (QUIT, a hypnotoad hot deployment, a worker reaching
      its accepts limit) no longer waits for graceful_timeout: the plugin
      closes its WebSocket connections as soon as the stop begins, with
      close code 1001. Clients reconnect by themselves and catch up. Under
      Docker this showed as a container that took its whole
      stop_grace_period to stop

    - BoardStreams::Client: when no channel has been joined for 30 seconds
      the client closes its connection (status "idle"), and the next join
      opens one again. The idle_delay option changes that time, and undef
      turns it off. The JavaScript client has the same change (idleDelay,
      in milliseconds; null turns it off)

v0.0.57 2026-11-26T11:03:22Z

    - BoardStreams::Client: every call of join now returns a channel object
      of its own. The objects for one channel share a single membership on
      the server, and the client leaves the channel when the last of them
      has left, so separate parts of a program no longer have to
      coordinate their leave calls. Code that joined a channel twice and
      left it once now stays joined until the second object leaves too.
      The JavaScript client has the same change

v0.0.56 2026-11-25T15:18:08Z

    - Server and clients now check a protocol version in place of the
      library version: a whole number, BoardStreams::PROTOCOL_VERSION,
      currently 1, which goes up only when a release makes the protocol
      incompatible with earlier ones. Library versions no longer have to
      match. The first heartbeat announces it as "protocol", and the
      reason for a refusal is now "protocol_mismatch"
    - INCOMPATIBLE: because the announcement itself changed, this release
      does not work with clients or servers of v0.0.55 and earlier

v0.0.55 2026-11-25T14:20:08Z

    - Added BoardStreams::Client, a Perl client that is a port of the
      JavaScript one: it connects over a WebSocket with Mojo::UserAgent
      and exposes channels through RxPerl observables and Mojo promises

v0.0.54 2026-11-25T07:27:20Z

    - A process announces the schema version it works with, and a process
      whose code only knows an older one stops serving when it hears that,
      instead of going on using upgraded tables the old way
    - Kicks, deletions and these announcements are now confined to the
      PostgreSQL schema that holds the tables, so that applications
      sharing a database no longer hear each other's

    - Added delete_channel, which deletes a channel's state and history
      and removes its members, telling them
    - Schema version 2, applied automatically: bs_event and bs_request now
      reference bs_channel with "on delete cascade" (rows left over from
      channels deleted by hand are removed by the migration), and a new
      table bs_floor keeps sequence numbers of deleted channels from
      being reused. New channels therefore no longer necessarily start
      at sequence number 0

v0.0.53 2026-11-25T01:04:49Z

    - Added kick_all, which removes every member from a channel

v0.0.52 2026-11-24T23:30:32Z

    - A server process that cannot receive PostgreSQL notifications now
      closes all its WebSocket connections and refuses new ones until it
      can, instead of keeping browsers connected and catching up later.
      It checks every listener_check_interval seconds (new option,
      default 5) that notifications still arrive. A PostgreSQL restart is
      therefore visible to browsers as a disconnection

    - Added kick and disconnect, on the hub (for all of a user's browsers,
      across server processes) and on the handler context (for the browser
      being served), and the "identify" plugin option that tells users
      apart. The JavaScript client does not reconnect after a disconnect

v0.0.51 2026-11-24T21:34:41Z

    - The first heartbeat of a connection now announces the version, and
      the JavaScript client refuses to work with a server of any other
      version (reason "version_mismatch"). Clients older than this change
      are not affected by it

    - Added the lazy_migrate plugin option, which postpones creating the
      tables until they are first needed
    - The tables are now also created on first use if PostgreSQL could not
      be reached at startup and update() is called before any browser
      connects

    "append" causes appends array exports from multiple searches using the 
    same variable to append (vs. overwrite) their values. default is old 
    behavior (i.e., "noappend" which overwrites).

    e.g., from t/10*t:

        FindBin::libs->import
        (
            qw
            (
                base=foo
                subdir=etc
                subonly
                export=etc
                append
            )
        );
        FindBin::libs->import
        (
            qw
            (
                base=bar
                subdir=etc
                subonly
                export=etc
                append
            )
        );

    generates:

        # Second pass looks for bar/etc:[
        #   '/sandbox/lembark/Modules/FindBin-libs/foo/etc',
        #   '/sandbox/lembark/Modules/FindBin-libs/bar/etc'
        # ]


    Main use is finding, say, multiple ./etc dir's and exporting
    them all into a search list for config files. 

    Given:

        ./myproj/etc
        ./shared/etc

    then #! code in ./myproj/bin could:

        use FindBin::libs qw( export base=etc                       );    
        use FindBin::libs qw( export base=shared subdir=etc subonly );

    and get @etc of ( .../myproj/etc, .../shared/etc ). 

    The old behavior, 'noappend' overwrites the variable (which can be
    handy for re-setting the dirs also).

****************************************************************
* Sereal 7 is a major release. Developers concerned with       *
* security or portability should upgrade as soon as possible.  *
*                                                              *
* Upgrade Sereal::Decoder to version 7 on every reader FIRST.  *
* Verify that rollout is complete before upgrading             *
* Sereal::Encoder to version 7 on any writer. V7 packets       *
* require a version 7 Decoder.                                 *
****************************************************************

7.008
    * Speed up scalar, string and small-varint encoding, and reduce
      stack usage by keeping larger helpers out of the hot path.
    * Reduce allocation overhead for dedupe_strings and
      aliased_dedupe_strings with a single C string table. Preserve
      binary/UTF-8 distinctions and reference tracking.
    * Reuse Zstd compression contexts on reusable encoders for payloads
      up to 512 KiB, avoiding repeated context allocation.
    * Improve buffer growth and container preallocation. Limit retained
      buffers on reusable encoders to 1 MiB after large payloads, and
      strengthen buffer size and overflow checks.
    * Preserve compression levels when FREEZE callbacks reuse the
      encoder.
    * Fix builds with assertions enabled on Perl 5.36 and later.
      Thanks to Steffen Mueller for these improvements and fixes.

7.007
    * Fix bundled Zstd build races under parallel make that can cause
      malformed archives and linker failures. Build the archive once
      before linking while preserving incremental rebuilds.
    * Exclude the archive itself and unrelated object files from its
      inputs. Replace existing archives to remove stale members.

7.006
    * Fix option lookup in cloned Perl threads, including children that
      outlive their parent thread. Give each interpreter its own option
      lookup data. Preserve builds with older Perl XS parsers.
    * Pass the actual remaining output buffer capacity to Snappy, Zlib
      and Zstd after writing packet headers and length prefixes. Add
      round-trip coverage across supported compression formats and
      protocol versions. Thanks to Steffen Mueller for both fixes.

7.005
    * Fix a false native long-double test failure on Intel macOS with
      older Perls. Use Config's myuname value to identify the CPU in the
      shared test. Encoding behavior is unchanged.

7.004
    * Update bundled zstd to 1.6.0, including upstream security fixes.
    * Update bundled miniz to 3.1.2.
    * Clarify checksum helper arguments, defaults and return values.
      Document the helpers as exportable functions after the methods.
      Explain when changes to defaults affect functions and objects.

7.003
    * Restore compilation on Perl builds without a U64 typedef,
      including reported 32-bit and older-Perl configurations.
    * Correct a false native long-double declaration test failure on
      older x86 macOS Perls.

7.002
    * Add an opt-in paranoid preset that requires a checksum key, uses
      IEEE double output, refuses objects by default, rejects unknown
      options, and limits recursion to 2048. Explicit constructor
      options can override each default.
    * Add allow_classes, refuse_objects and track_classes for object
      policy and per-class counts. Permit genuine Regexp objects through
      refuse_objects; croak_on_bless still rejects them.
    * Add allow_unsigned as an explicit checksum-policy opt-out. Lower
      the normal recursion limit from 10000 to 8192, or 4096 on Cygwin.
      Document the preset's precision and callback implications.
    * Traverse XPerl hash storage through its entry API.
    * Balance custom-op result references on Perl builds with
      PERL_RC_STACK.
    * Fix native floating-point declaration tests on older FreeBSD and
      macOS Perls. Make the magical-array child test portable on Windows.

7.001
    * Use protocol v7 by default, with portable little-endian IEEE
      floating-point storage. Extended values use IEEE binary128 by
      default, including on long-double Perl builds.
    * Add float_type (std/native) for explicit native long-double
      output. Declare the native format, byte order and storage size
      once per document, and clear known padding. Unidentified layouts
      support explicitly trusted same-build round trips.
    * Preserve protocol v1-v6 numeric output behavior and keep v7 header
      floats portable. Upgrade Decoder to version 7 before emitting v7
      packets.
    * Include protocol v6 support for v-strings, negative-integer
      encoding and keyed SipHash checksums. Add checksum keys, modes,
      policies, shared and module-specific defaults, and
      prepare_checksum_key().
    * Preserve regexp character-set modifiers, /n and /xx, and improve
      unsupported-type diagnostics.
    * Preserve unsigned tied integer values on older Perls and
      strengthen callback lifetime handling.
    * Fix bundled Snappy builds on Haiku and hobodecoder compatibility
      with BusyBox od. Improve older-Perl and optional-dependency
      handling.
    * Extend hobodecoder and stored corpus coverage for portable and
      native floats. Include real Fedora s390x producer captures for
      regression tests. Thanks to pghmcfc for the report and corpus
      (issue #337).
    * Ship the shared SECURITY policy and clarify security, checksum and
      floating-point interoperability documentation.

6.003
    * Fix bundled Snappy builds on Haiku, which has no byteswap.h.
    * Use portable od arguments in hobodecoder for BusyBox systems and
      report signal termination correctly in checksum tests.

6.002
    * Preserve unsigned tied integer values on older Perls instead of
      converting their private cached values through a signed integer.
    * Keep sorted-key wire expectations independent of Perl's temporary
      hash reference counts.
    * Report the actual missing dependency when skipping t/400_evil.t.
    * Skip only hobodecoder decompression checks when its optional
      Compress::Zlib dependency is unavailable, and show child errors.

6.001
    * Add protocol v6 support for VSTRING extension tags, NEG_VARINT, and
      keyed SipHash checksums. Upgrade Decoder to version 6 throughout the
      fleet before emitting v6 packets.
    * Add checksum_key, checksum_key_v1/v2/v3, checksum_mode, and
      checksum_policy options, shared and Encoder-specific defaults, and
      prepare_checksum_key().
    * Preserve regexp character set modifiers, /n, and /xx. Upgrade Decoder
      before emitting these modifiers.
    * Ship a SECURITY policy in release archives and improve the protocol
      specification, diagnostics, build and compatibility tests, and
      general robustness.
    * Reported fixes: regexp modifiers
      (https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/issues/180 and
      https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/issues/262), and unsupported-type
      diagnostics (https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/issues/191).
      Related work: specification
      (https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/issues/218) and packaged security
      policy (https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/issues/305).
    * Thanks to Matt Koscica and Oz Kaiser (@tatikoma), with assistance from
      Claude Code and Codex.

5.011
    * Robustness fixes. Thanks to Steffen Mueller and kumar-Prakash07.
    * Preserve zstd deprecation warnings when building with IBM XL C on AIX.
    * Raise the minimum supported Perl version to 5.14.
    * Fix the Sereal::Decoder prerequisite version in generated package metadata.
      See https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/issues/317

5.010
    * Released to match Decoder version.

5.009
    * Only use Perl's C<$Config{ccflags}> when building bundled zstd on
      AIX / IBM toolchains, or when C<SEREAL_ZSTD_USE_CONFIG_CCFLAGS> is
      set. Other platforms now use the normal zstd build flags again.

5.008

5.007

5.006

5.005

5.004

5.003

7.008
    * Improve Encoder and Decoder performance with faster scalar and
      varint handling, more efficient string deduplication, and reuse of
      Zstd contexts. Reduce Encoder buffer allocation and retention.
    * Preserve compression, readonly and integer aliasing settings when
      FREEZE/THAW callbacks reuse their encoder or decoder.

      make, including malformed archives and linker failures. Preserve
      incremental rebuilds and exclude stale or unrelated archive
      members.

      including children that outlive their parent thread. Preserve
      builds with older Perl XS parsers.

      and Zstd compression. Thanks to Steffen Mueller for both fixes.

* Sereal::Encoder to version 7 on any writer. V7 packets       *
* require a version 7 Decoder.                                 *
****************************************************************

7.008
    * Speed up small-varint decoding and arrays of untracked scalar
      values. Reduce temporary allocations and stack usage while
      preserving recursion limits, aliasing and readonly options.
    * Reuse Zstd decompression contexts on reusable decoders instead of
      allocating a context for each packet.
    * Preserve readonly and integer aliasing options when THAW callbacks
      reuse the decoder.
    * Avoid calling is_utf8_string() with zero-length inputs when
      validating empty UTF-8 strings and hash keys.
      Thanks to Steffen Mueller for these improvements and fixes.
    * Keep Zstd regression coverage active with older or absent Encoders
      by using stored packets for Decoder tests.

7.007
    * Fix bundled Zstd build races under parallel make that can cause
      malformed archives and linker failures. Build the archive once
      before linking while preserving incremental rebuilds.
    * Exclude the archive itself and unrelated object files from its
      inputs. Replace existing archives to remove stale members.

7.006
    * Fix option lookup in cloned Perl threads, including children that
      outlive their parent thread. Give each interpreter its own option
      lookup data. Preserve builds with older Perl XS parsers.
      Thanks to Steffen Mueller.

7.005
    * Fix a false native long-double test failure on Intel macOS with
      older Perls. Use Config's myuname value to identify the CPU and
      recognize compatible native packets. Decoding behavior is unchanged.

7.004
    * Update bundled zstd to 1.6.0, including upstream security fixes.
    * Update bundled miniz to 3.1.2, including guards against inflate
      infinite loops on invalid Huffman codes.
    * Add invalid-Huffman regression tests that check packet rejection
      and decoder reuse. Accept decompression errors from older external
      miniz libraries without requiring a particular error code.
    * Correct the documented default key order for
      validate_sereal_checksum() and the interaction between
      no_bless_objects and no_thaw_objects.
    * Clarify checksum helper arguments, defaults and return values.
      Document the helpers as exportable functions after the methods.
      Explain when changes to defaults affect functions and objects.

7.003
    * Correct a false native long-double declaration test failure on
      older x86 macOS Perls.

7.002
    * Add an opt-in paranoid preset for authenticated input, bounded
      decompression and container sizes, UTF-8 validation, restricted
      object blessing and THAW, and a recursion limit of 2048. Explicit
      constructor options can override each default.
    * Add allow_classes for ordinary and frozen objects and
      track_classes for per-class object counts. Permit genuine Regexp
      objects through refuse_objects unless an allowlist excludes them.
    * Add allow_unsigned as an explicit checksum-policy opt-out. Lower
      the normal recursion limit from 10000 to 8192, or 4096 on Cygwin.
      Clarify the trust assumptions and limits of paranoid mode.
    * Balance custom-op argument and result references on Perl builds
      with PERL_RC_STACK.
    * Fix native floating-point declaration tests on older FreeBSD and
      macOS Perls. Remove hobodecoder's od dependency and make child
      tests portable on Windows. Bound randomized test runtime and TAP
      memory use, and adapt deep-recursion tests to Cygwin's stack.

7.001
    * Read protocol versions 1 through 7. Decode portable little-endian
      v7 floats, including IEEE binary128 on Perl builds without
      quadmath, converting values to the local NV type.
    * Validate v7 native long-double declarations and reject known
      format, byte-order and size mismatches. Add
      allow_unknown_long_double for explicitly trusted same-build reads
      of unidentified layouts; storage sizes must still match.
    * Preserve native floating-point behavior for protocol v1-v6 input.
      Add legacy_float_byteorder for older data with a known source byte
      order.
    * Include protocol v6 v-string and negative-integer support, keyed
      SipHash verification, checksum keys, modes, policies and defaults.
      Add prepare_checksum_key(), get_sereal_checksum() and
      validate_sereal_checksum().
    * Restore regexp character-set modifiers, /n and /xx, and report the
      required Perl version for unsupported modifiers.
    * Harden malformed-input and object handling. Retain Decoder handles
      across callbacks, and run output DESTROY callbacks before
      capturing input on Perl 5.24.
    * Restore older-Perl builds, avoid read-only regexp buffer
      corruption on Perl 5.14, and correct 32-bit size handling and
      allocation diagnostics.
    * Fix bundled Snappy builds on Haiku and hobodecoder compatibility
      with BusyBox od. Improve optional-dependency diagnostics.
    * Extend independent wire-format and stored corpus coverage,
      including real Fedora s390x producer captures. Add a
      floating-point corpus collector and named declarations in
      diagnostics and hobodecoder. Thanks to pghmcfc for the report and
      corpus (issue #337).
    * Ship the shared SECURITY policy and clarify security, checksum and
      floating-point interoperability documentation.

6.003
    * Fix bundled Snappy builds on Haiku, which has no byteswap.h.
    * Use portable od arguments in hobodecoder for BusyBox systems and
      report signal termination correctly in checksum tests.

6.002
    * Keep the Decoder alive when a callback clears its handle variable,
      preventing use-after-free during decoding and cleanup.
    * Restore builds on older supported Perls without SSize_t_MAX.
    * Run output DESTROY callbacks before capturing the input buffer on
      Perl 5.24, matching other supported Perls.
    * Avoid corrupting regexp buffers during read-only cleanup on Perl 5.14.
    * Inspect undef aliases without creating writable slots on older Perls.
      Account for Perl 5.14/5.16's regexp-copy lifetime limitation in tests.
    * Fix huge-size test expectations for 32-bit Perls with 64-bit integers
      and format allocation diagnostics with the correct argument types.
    * Skip only hobodecoder decompression checks when its optional
      Compress::Zlib dependency is unavailable, and show child errors.
    * Report the actual missing dependency when skipping t/400_evil.t.

6.001
    * Read protocol v6 VSTRING extension tags, NEG_VARINT, and keyed
      SipHash checksums while retaining support for older packets.
    * Add checksum_key, checksum_key_v1/v2/v3, checksum_mode, and
      checksum_policy options, shared and Decoder-specific defaults,
      prepare_checksum_key(), get_sereal_checksum(), and
      validate_sereal_checksum().
    * Restore regexp matching modifiers, including /n and /xx, and report
      the required Perl version for unsupported modifiers.
    * Ship a SECURITY policy in release archives and improve the protocol
      specification, build and mixed-version compatibility tests, and
      general robustness.
    * Reported fixes: regexp modifiers
      (https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/issues/180 and
      https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/issues/262).
      Related work: specification
      (https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/issues/218) and packaged security
      policy (https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/issues/305).
    * Thanks to Matt Koscica and Oz Kaiser (@tatikoma), with assistance from
      Claude Code and Codex.

5.011

5.010
    * Reset the pending frozen-object state (thaw_av and ref_thawhash) at the
      start of every decode. A decode that died before srl_finalize_structure
      ran -- a truncated document, for example -- left those populated, and the
      next decode on the same decoder then thawed items belonging to the failed
      document and looked up ref_thawhash keys pointing at freed AVs. That
      segfaulted or silently produced the wrong class.
      See https://github.com/Sereal/Sereal/pull/316

        1): closefrom N becomes a close of each fd from N up that the

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

## [v0.1.7] - 2026-11-28

All about the benchmarks this time.

### Changed

- Remove always-on scheduler bookkeeping to tidy up our hot path:
  - Skip priority scans and disabled `maybe_yield()` calls
  - Track live fibers incrementally
  - Gate diagnostic counters
  - Keep park/queue state in pre-sized fiber slots
  - Use raw fiber lookups plus a shared `['WAITING']` marker on the park/resume path.
- Eliminate repeated C job-pool scans and lock churn:
  - Maintain pending counts and free/pending/sleep bitmaps
  - Drain completions under one lock
  - Merge completion publication with the next claim
  - Deliver results in a flat buffer
- Make short waits cheaper without turning long idle periods into busy loops:
  - Bounded sub-millisecond polling after job activity
  - Longer fast-poll budget
  - Wall clock spin windows for sub-tick sleeps
  - High res `yield` spin for Windows sleeps up to 8 ms
- Reduce startup and virtual-timer work with a single fiber-table scan/call and ordered timers using a compacted fired prefix and parallel deadline/fiber arrays instead of per-timer arrayrefs.
- Trim common wait/cleanup paths by inlining the usual `Channel::get()`/`put()` case, skipping fiber-local cleanup when no locals exist and stopping backtrace capture at the first library frame.

### Fixed

- Size the high-volume driver tests against the descriptors they actually allocate, so a platform with more than the assumed 16 pre-existing handles (NetBSD 11, whose `FD_SETSIZE` is 256) no longer parks a read on an unnameable fd and loses a wakeup. (https://matrix.perl-magpie.org/results/e76ea43a-e600-11f1-83c9-deb385cf8ea6)

## [v0.1.6] - 2026-11-20

### Fixed

- On GNU/Hurd, cap the default fiber limit at 512 when `RLIMIT_DATA` is unlimited (as it often is there, with the real ceiling coming from the Mach task or physical memory) instead of leaving it at 65536 and letting the first large burst fail with an mmap error.
- Builder should only link `-lperl` when an unversioned `libperl` is actually present in the perl's `CORE` dir.

## [v0.1.5] - 2026-11-20

### Fixed

- Request `_LARGEFILE64_SOURCE` before including `perl.h`, so its `off64_t` alias resolves under `-D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64`.
- GNU/Hurd and Cygwin both use 2 MiB fiber stacks and clamp there instead of allowing a handful of 8 MiB stacks to exhaust the data-segment budget.
- Enforce `with_timeout()` at the block boundary so a result that lands after the deadline throws `Error::Timeout` even when a busy host fires the timer helper late.
- Don't double-fail a deadline that was already delivered at a park.
- Several fixes for Cygwin:
  - Fiber stacks now come from `VirtualAlloc` (with a `PAGE_NOACCESS` guard page) and the initial ucontext is armed directly instead of through `makecontext()`. Cygwin's `mmap()` can't commit pages from inside a ucontext and its `makecontext()` jumps to `uc_link` rather than returning when called from one, which silently prevented nested fibers from ever running.
  - Warm the socket layer on the main stack at initialization. Cygwin's first `socket()` call initializes Winsock lazily and fails with `EINVAL` when made from a fiber's ucontext, which makes `IO::Socket::INET->new()` return `undef`.
  - `spawn_blocking_fork()` now croaks with a clear message instead of killing the whole process because Cygwin can't `fork()` from a fiber stack. Cygwin perls have ithreads and should use `spawn_blocking()` anyway.

## [v0.1.1] - 2026-10-25

Borrowing patterns from Rust, Erlang, Java, etc. to bring more familiar concurrency primitives to Parataxis. No real changes to the core this time.

### Added

- `Acme::Parataxis::Blocking`: CPU offloading onto a bounded pool of cloned interpreters via `spawn_blocking` (lazily loads threads/shared modules on first use).
- `spawn_blocking_fork`: Process-based CPU offloading for non-ithreads Perls with IPC via `Storable`, bounded worker pools, and signal-based cancellation via `kill_blocking_fork`.
- `Acme::Parataxis::Actor`: Mailbox-driven actors with bounded queues, backpressure, `ask` (returning a `Future`), `send`, and graceful teardown.
- `Acme::Parataxis::Supervisor`: OTP-style supervision trees supporting `OneForOne`, `OneForAll`, and `RestForOne` restart strategies with configurable restart budgets.
- Synchronization primitives:
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Sync::Mutex`: Non-reentrant lock with strict FIFO hand-off and ownership tracking.
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Sync::RwLock`: Writer-preferring, reentrant read/write lock.
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Sync::WaitGroup`: Fiber job counter (`add`, `done`, `wait`).
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Sync::Barrier`: Reusable phase rendezvous point.
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Sync::Once`: Race-safe, single-execution initializer.
- Structured concurrency & flow control:
  - `nursery( sub ($n) { ... } )`: Structured fiber scopes where child errors cancel siblings and propagate outward.
  - `pmap( { concurrency => $n, }, sub ( $item ) { ... }, @items )`: Parallel list mapping over a bounded fiber pool.
  - `with_timeout( $ms, [ $token, ] $code )` and `with_cancel( $code )`: Cooperative deadline and cancellation scopes.
  - `Acme::Parataxis::CancellationToken`: Cooperative park-interrupt token.
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Local`: Fiber-local ambient storage.
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Generator`: Stackful, lazy pull iterator.
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Monitor`: Non-owning fiber observer.
- Channels & Streams:
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Channel::select`: CSP-style waiting across multiple channels with random case selection to prevent starvation.
  - `try_get` / `try_put` non-blocking channel operations and per-channel timeout configurations.
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Stream`: Backpressure-driven channel pipelines (`map`, `filter`, `batch`, `batch_time`, `throttle`).
  - `Acme::Parataxis::Ticker`: Drift-free interval timer.
  - `Acme::Parataxis::RateLimiter`: Token bucket limiter driven by `Ticker`.
- Software Transactional Memory (STM): `Acme::Parataxis::TVar` cells and `atomically` transactions with conflict detection and `retry()`.
- Future combinators: `wait_all` and `wait_any`.
- Event loop & OS integration:
  - Event loop drivers: `Acme::Parataxis::Driver::Mojo` and `Acme::Parataxis::Driver::IOAsync`.
  - Transparent unblocking (`Acme::Parataxis::Compat`): Opt-in cooperative `CORE::GLOBAL` overrides for `sleep`, `read`, and `sysread`.
  - Deterministic virtual clock via `run( virtual => 1 )` and `advance( $ms )`.
  - Graceful shutdown handlers via `run( on_shutdown => ... )` for `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`.
  - `fd_setsize()` introspection helper.
- Diagnostics & Introspection:
  - `dump_fibers()` and backtrace-rich deadlock diagnostics.
  - New exceptions: `Acme::Parataxis::Error`, `Error::Cancelled`, and `Error::Timeout`.
  - Verified Perl `defer` compatibility within fiber scopes.

### Fixed

- Event loop drivers now key watches by handle identity rather than recycled file descriptor numbers, eliminating lost wakeups and orphaned slots.
- Fixed non-numeric string values being silently accepted in `Supervisor->new( within => ... )`.
- Fiber jump environments (`PL_top_env`) are now preserved across context switches, preventing crashes (`0xC0000005`) when completion callbacks throw.
- Blessed exceptions stringifying to empty strings (e.g. `Error::Timeout`) are no longer misidentified as clean exits.
- Fixed bare `Died at ...` rethrows in `run()` and `Channel->get` when evaluated blocks or messages return falsey values (`0`, `''`).
- Deadlock detection now resets scheduler run queues and state so subsequent runs remain usable.
- Awaited fiber crashes are now caught and rethrown by `await` rather than killing the entire scheduler loop.
- `await_sleep` now uses native condition variable timed waits (`pthread_cond_timedwait`, `SleepConditionVariableCS`) instead of 4ms polling.
- Context switches now strictly maintain canonical `AvREIFY_only` state on argument pads, fixing `Perl_pp_entersub` assertions on `DEBUGGING` builds.
- Fiber-parking primitives now clean up `@_` landing pads before parking to avoid cross-fiber pad pollution.
- `submit_c_job` now broadcasts condition variables to prevent queued jobs from stalling behind unrelated worker sleeps.
- Enforced platform `FD_SETSIZE` bounds checks on worker pool read/write jobs and event-loop watches to prevent stack buffer overflows.
- Prevented uninitialized memory bugs in BSD `get_cpu_count` sysctl lookups.
- `exit()` from inside yielded fibers is now safely trapped and re-raised across all platforms.
- Fixed pad argument and buffer truncation when multiple fibers park inside the same shared subroutine.
- Resolved `Can't undef active subroutine` when disabling `Acme::Parataxis::Compat` by correctly cleaning up fabricated `CvDEPTH` frames.
- Corrected C function signature for `para_release_cv_depth` under Affix on Windows.

- Traversed nested runlevels (`si_prev`/`si_next`) during depth settlement to prevent `cx_popsub_args` assertion failures inside test subtest blocks.

### Changed

- Maximum fiber limits are now dynamic: configurable via `max_fibers()` and `set_max_fibers()`.
- Increased default fiber limit from 1,024 to 65,536.

## [v0.1.0] - 2026-09-21

This started as a silly little diversion in February but I'm using this in actual projects now. I've even used it to shake out bugs in Affix.

I might move it out of the Acme namespace...

Anyway, the major win is that fiber hot path has been moved from Perl into C and roughly tripled context swapping throughput with no change to the public API.

### Added

- `Acme::Parataxis::Channel`: a buffered FIFO message queue for producer/consumer patterns between fibers. Writers block when full, readers when empty; a capacity of `1` makes it a rendezvous point. Built on two semaphores.
- `Acme::Parataxis::Future`: a one-shot placeholder for an eventual computation result. A producer fires `set_result`/`set_error` exactly once; consumers pick it up with `await`/`result` or register an `on_ready` callback.
- `Acme::Parataxis::Semaphore`: a counting semaphore with no ownership: blocked fibers are parked (no busy-wait) and resumed FIFO as permits become available.
- `Acme::Parataxis::Signal`: a two-state flag with a FIFO queue of waiters. `send` latches the signal so a later `wait` consumes it immediately, while `broadcast` wakes every queued waiter at once (and drops if nobody is waiting).

### Fixed

- Fixed crash (double-free / use-after-free) when fibers call Affix'd functions on non-threaded Perl. The bug was in Affix's `SAVEVPTR`/`SAVEDESTRUCTOR_X` arena pattern, which was not fiber-safe; now fixed upstream in Affix v1.2.5+.
- Fixed SIGSEGV on macOS and FreeBSD caused by fiber stacks being only 512KB (via `posix_memalign`). All POSIX platforms now use a 64MB `mmap`-backed stack with a PROT_NONE guard page, matching the Linux path. The SIGSEGV guard handler is also available on macOS/FreeBSD now.
- Fixed FreeBSD compilation: added `MAP_ANONYMOUS` w/ `MAP_ANON` fallback.
- Fixed macOS SIGBUS: the guard region size is now derived from `sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE)` at runtime so it always covers at least one full page (16 KiB on Apple Silicon). Also fixed `cleanup()` to use `munmap()` instead of `free()` on non-Linux POSIX platforms.
- `is_finished()` now rejects fiber ids of `MAX_FIBERS` or greater instead of reading out of bounds of the fiber table.
- Closed a busy-spin footgun: `wait`, fiber `await`, `Semaphore` waits, and `Signal->wait` now croak instead of burning 100% CPU when called from outside the scheduler, and `->new` croaks when the 1024-slot fiber table is exhausted rather than creating a fiber that can never run.
- A fiber that yields during its initial run is now re-enqueued by the scheduler instead of being dropped, which previously could hang a regex-heavy workload.
- The scheduler no longer hangs when a fiber object is created but never spawned (`->new` without `spawn`): live-fiber tracking only counts fibers that have actually started, matching Coro's ready-queue semantics.
- `async`/`run` is now re-entrant: a nested `async` inside another `async` or inside a fiber shares the one run loop (like Coro's single global scheduler) and returns the block's value, instead of clobbering the outer scheduler and deadlocking.
- A destroyed fiber's id is kept out of the free list until every job it submitted has been reclaimed, so a stale completion can never be misdelivered to a (or corrupt) fiber that later reuses the id.
- Pending-job tracking now reads the C-side outstanding job count instead of a run-local counter, so jobs left over from a `stop`ped run are drained and handled by the next run instead of tripping `FATAL: deadlock detected` or sitting in the done-queue forever.
- `Semaphore` `up`/`adjust` skip stale (already destroyed) waiters instead of consuming a wake that should go to a live fiber.
- Channel constructors now reject a capacity below 1 instead of deadlocking on it at load time.
- The 1024-slot job queue is no longer fatal on the first try: `_submit_job` yields once and retries before croaking.
- `Future::set_result`/`set_error` wake awaiters exactly once instead of appending a duplicate `_wake_waiters` callback on every `await`.

### Changed

- Spawned fibers run inline at spawn time.
- The fiber registry is replaced by strong references to each fiber object in C.
- Fiber completion moved from a Perl method into C: the entry point writes state directly into the object's slots with `av_store`, and only dispatches callbacks when callbacks were actually registered.
- To save time on FFI boundary crossings, `spawn` now performs the whole create run sequence in a single call and builds the fiber object in C.
- Fiber objects are incrementally-filled AV*s instead of HV*s.
- On x86_64 ELF, context switching uses a hand written trampoline that only saves the callee-saved registers and stack pointer, avoiding `swapcontext`'s signal-mask syscall.
- `spawn` and `await` hot paths flattened by inlining helpers.
- Worker threads block on `select()` for the full `await_read`/`await_write` timeout instead of polling every 10ms, cutting idle syscalls by ~50x. On POSIX a shutdown pipe wakes any worker blocked in `select()` during `cleanup()`.

        1.511:
        - faster HTTP/2, TLS and native paths; less memory on big or idle TLS
        - timer-made writes are sent when the timer returns; no handle DESTROY
        - fix: re-listening right after unlisten() could spin the event loop

1.509 Tue Oct 20 14:54:11 2026 +0300
        - security and robustness hardening across HTTP/1, HTTP/2 and TLS
        - enforce retired generation drain deadlines through reload and shutdown

1.507 Fri Sep 25 10:49:04 2026 +0300
        New:
        - multiple server instances (new_instance) and multiple listeners
          per instance, IPv6 among them
        - TLS 1.3 via picotls+openssl: per-listener certificates, SNI vhosts
        - HTTP/2 via nghttp2: multiplexing, streaming, extended CONNECT
          (RFC 8441), rapid-reset (CVE-2023-44487) and ping-flood
          (CVE-2019-9512) protection
        - PROXY protocol v1/v2, including TLVs
        - reverse_proxy mode: take client_address and url_scheme from
          X-Forwarded-For/-Proto behind a trusted upstream; off by default
        - SO_REUSEPORT, sendfile
        - timeouts and limits: header_timeout, write_timeout, linger_timeout,
          max_connections, max_body_len, max_uri_len, max_read_buf,
          max_accept_per_loop, max_h2_concurrent_streams, max_h2_conn_body,
          wbuf_low_water
        - introspection: active_conns, total_requests, access_log,
          pause_accept/resume_accept, set_psgix_io
        - psgix.h2.trailers, psgix.h2.extended_connect, psgix.h2.protocol,
          psgix.proxy_tlvs
        - psgi.input gains getline, getlines and <$fh>
        - Feersum::Runner: hot_restart, preload_app, daemonize, pid_file,
          user/group, after_fork, access_log, graceful_timeout,
          startup_timeout, max_requests_per_worker
        - bin/feersum native mode with full Runner option parity

        Incompatible with 1.505:
        - requires Perl 5.14 (was 5.8.7)
        - the Feersum object is no longer a hashref; use the public API
        - psgix.input.buffered is no longer advertised (psgi.input is
          forward-only; Plack buffers the body when it is unset)
        - a UTF8-flagged response string whose characters all fit in a byte
          is sent as those bytes, like every other PSGI server
        - a 1xx final status is refused (101 excepted); a status above 599
          answers 500
        - CR or LF in the status line, and a control character in a response
          header (a tab is allowed in a value), are refused (CWE-113)
        - psgi.input is always present, per PSGI 1.1
        - a graceful stop, worker retirement and hot-restart handover exit
          via POSIX::_exit: END blocks do not run and buffered STDOUT is
          lost (set $| = 1 or log to STDERR)

        See the UPGRADING section in the docs for behaviour changes that
        bite with no code change (tighter default limits among them).

  - Fix default PRNG seeding (previous setup(rand()) truncated to seed 0)
    by seeding from native OS entropy (BCryptGenRandom/RtlGenRandom on
    Windows, /dev/urandom on Unix) with a 32-bit-safe fallback that
    preserves $!, and automatically reseed the default RNG after fork()
    as well as ithreads CLONE.

    are preserved on 32-bit-IV Perls.

    cs_select() and derived order statistics, and reject NaN in
    confidence level and approx_erf_inv() domain guards.
  - Prevent signed 32-bit multiplication overflow in third_quartile() on
    very large samples.
  - Upgrade mean() to Neumaier compensated summation with overflow-safe
    incremental fallback; upgrade standard deviation functions to scaled
    single-pass summation (avoiding overflow/underflow) and allow optional
    1-argument calling form sample_standard_deviation(\@sample) and
    population_standard_deviation(\@sample).

    and Acklam + Halley normal quantile refinement for full double
    precision across extreme tails.

    - Distinguish nested required arrays from the property-level required extension.
    - Enforce max_errors when merging alternative branch errors and interpret zero

      schemas, correct conditional syntax, string lengths and array item offsets.
    - Honour the default minimum of one contains match even when maxContains is set.

v0.6.0 2025-11-25T19:17:41+0900
    [New Features]
    - Added compile_js() to generate a standalone JavaScript validator from the
      current schema. The generated code exposes a single global function:
          validate(inst) -> [ { path, keyword, message, schema_pointer }, ... ]
      using the same error structure as the Perl engine.
    - compile_js() supports an 'ecma' option:
          ecma => "auto"    # default; cautious feature detection
          ecma => 2018      # assume ES2018+ (Unicode property escapes, /u, etc.)
      allowing callers to tune how aggressively Unicode regexp features are used
      in the generated JavaScript.

    [JavaScript Codegen]
    - Implemented a conservative Perl-regexp to JavaScript converter for
      'pattern' keywords:
          * \x{...}  -> \uHHHH / \u{HHHHH}
          * \p{Katakana}, \p{Hiragana}, \p{Han}, etc. -> \p{scx=...}
        with proper escaping for use inside new RegExp("...","u").
      Patterns that cannot be compiled by the browser are safely skipped on the
      client and remain enforced by the Perl validator.
    - JavaScript validator now covers:
          type, const (primitive), enum,
          minLength / maxLength / pattern,
          minimum / maximum / exclusiveMinimum / exclusiveMaximum,
          minItems / maxItems / items (single-schema form),
          contains / minContains / maxContains,
          properties / required,
          allOf / anyOf / oneOf / not,
          if / then / else,
          and the non-core 'uniqueKeys' applicator when enabled in Perl.
      Negative "not + required" patterns are deliberately skipped client-side and
      enforced server-side only, to avoid surprising UX.

    [Behaviour Changes]
    - For generated JavaScript only: when numeric bound keywords are present
      (minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum), numeric-looking
      strings such as "10" or "3.14" are coerced to numbers before applying
      the bounds. Non-numeric values:
          * raise a 'type' error ("expected number but found ...") when no
            explicit 'type' is declared, or
          * are checked by the schema's 'type' keyword when present.
      This provides friendlier form validation in browsers while the Perl
      engine remains strictly JSON-typed.
    - Ensured error locations and schema pointers reported by the generated
      JavaScript match the Perl engine, so server-side and client-side logs
      can be correlated easily.

    [Documentation & Tests]
    - Expanded POD to document compile_js(), its 'ecma' option, the JavaScript
      error format, and typical integration in web forms.

    [Core Implementation]
    - Full support for JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, including:
        * $id / $anchor / $ref with external & fragment resolution,
        * $dynamicAnchor / $dynamicRef with correct dynamic scope lookup.
    - Recursion safety implemented via (schema_pointer, instance_address) pairs.
    - Comprehensive keyword coverage: type (including unions with inline schemas),
      const, enum, multipleOf (float-tolerant), numeric bounds, length and pattern,
      prefixItems/items, contains(min/max), uniqueItems, unevaluatedItems,
      properties / patternProperties / additionalProperties, propertyNames,
      required / dependentRequired / dependentSchemas, unevaluatedProperties,
      allOf / anyOf / oneOf / not, and if/then/else.
    - Unevaluated* keyword handling uses annotation tracking on evaluated nodes
      (props/items maps), matching spec semantics.

    [New Features]
    - Optional ahead-of-time compilation:
        * Enables fast-path validation via closures per schema node.
        * Use ->compile() or constructor 'compile => 1'.
        * Indexes anchors / dynamic anchors for constant-time lookup.
    - Content assertions (RFC 8927):
        * Enable via ->content_checks() or constructor 'content_assert => 1'.
        * Supports contentEncoding (built-in base64), contentMediaType,
          pluggable media decoders, and contentSchema validation.
        * Ships with 'application/json' decoder/validator.
    - Built-in format validators:
        * Activate via ->register_builtin_formats().
        * Provides validators for date/time/duration (ISO8601), email/idn-email,
          hostname/idn-hostname, IPv4/IPv6, URI/IRI/URI-reference, UUID,
          JSON Pointer / Relative JSON Pointer, and regex.
        * Custom format handlers via ->register_format() or constructor 'format => {}'.
    - Tracing and introspection:
        * Enable via ->trace().
        * Limit / sample with ->trace_limit() and ->trace_sample().
        * Retrieve via ->get_trace() (returns a copy).
    - Vocabulary enforcement:
        * Honors $vocabulary and required entries.
        * Unknown vocabularies may be ignored via ->ignore_unknown_required_vocab().

    [API Additions]
    - Constructor options:
        compile, content_assert, format (hash reference of callbacks),
        ignore_unknown_required_vocab, max_errors, normalize_instance,
        trace, trace_limit, trace_sample, vocab_support (hash reference).
    - Methods:
        compile(), content_checks(), enable_content_checks(),
        ignore_unknown_required_vocab(),
        register_content_decoder(), register_format(),
        register_media_validator(), set_resolver(), set_vocabulary_support(),
        trace(), trace_limit(), trace_sample().
      Accessors: is_* variants and get_trace_limit().
    - Error handling:
        ->error() returns the first JSON::Schema::Validate::Error object
        (stringifies to '"path: message"').
        ->errors() returns an array reference (up to max_errors).

    [Behavioral Improvements]
    - Instance normalisation (enabled by default): round-trips values to enforce
      strict JSON typing distinct from Perl dual values. Can be disabled via
      'normalize_instance => 0'.

    [Bug Fixes & Polish]
    - Added missing dependency declarations (thanks Slaven Rezić, GitLab #1).
    - Numeric strictness now based on B::FLAGS (IOK/NOK) for correct JSON semantics.
    - UTF-8-aware string lengths via codepoint iteration (not bytes).
    - All mutator methods return $self for chained configuration.

    [Documentation & Tests]
    - Expanded POD: constructor options, method semantics, formats, normalisation,
      vocabulary behaviour, recursion notes, unevaluated* examples.
    - Test suite now covers: dynamic anchors, external refs, combinators,
      unevaluated*, content/media assertions, compile vs interpretive modes,
      trace output, vocabulary validation, and structured errors.

0.001.0	Thu Nov 26 09:16:20 PM EST 2026
	First release.

	- One backend process holds one object per client connection, so a class
	  is loaded once and every process calls the same instance.  A frontend
	  forwards method calls and keeps calling context without loading the
	  class.
	- Transports: a unix domain socket, mode 0600 inside a directory only its
	  owner can write to; or TCP over TLS 1.2 or later, with a client
	  certificate at each end and an HMAC-SHA-256 token on every frame.
	- A connection accepts one hello.  A second is refused rather than
	  changing the class under objects it already holds.
	- Bounded resources: frame size, per-client and total queued data, buffer
	  memory, log size, and call, read, write, handshake and idle timeouts.
	  Large or deeply nested requests are thawed in a child first.
	- class-shared start, status, stop and path, including --max-memory.
	- Requires perl 5.026.  The backend is Unix-only; Class::Shared::Protocol
	  is portable and can talk to a backend elsewhere.
	- Test suite: 1274 tests, including state-transition, TLS, queueing,
	  security, first-time-user and real-class integration tests.

0.003.1	Fri Nov 27 09:50:06 PM EST 2026
	[ Bug Fixes ]
	- Parser: the Triplet token was ignored when computing durations, so
	  triplet notes, chords and rests lasted their full written value and
	  bars containing them were too long.  They now last two thirds of it.
	- MusicXML: triplets printed as plain notes.  <time-modification> and
	  <tuplet> elements are now emitted.
	- bin/nwc2musicxml still reported version 0.002.3.

0.003.0	Mon Nov  9 08:17:51 PM EST 2026
	[ Bug Fixes ]
	- MusicXML: a whole rest standing alone in a bar was emitted as a
	  four-crotchet rest whatever the time signature, so bars in 7/8, 3/4,
	  2/4 etc. were the wrong length and importers re-barred or padded the
	  music.  NWC uses a whole rest to mean "rest for the whole bar"; it is
	  now emitted as <rest measure="yes"/> with the duration of the bar.
	  <divisions> is raised where needed so the bar length is a whole
	  number of ticks.

	[ Enhancements ]
	- Added website

0.002.4	Tue Nov  3 04:12:32 PM EST 2026
	[ Bug Fixes ]
	- MusicXML: DynVariance events (Style:Crescendo / Style:Diminuendo) were
	  incorrectly emitted as hairpin wedge elements (<wedge type="crescendo"/
	  <wedge type="diminuendo"/>).  DynVariance records represent written text
	  markings ("cresc.", "dim.") not hairpins; hairpins come from
	  Opts:Crescendo/Opts:Diminuendo on individual notes.  DynVariance is now
	  emitted as <words font-style="italic">cresc.</words> or
	  <words font-style="italic">dim.</words>.  Style:crescOff now correctly
	  emits nothing (no stop element needed for a text marking).
	- Parser: Text events with a Pos field but no Placement field defaulted to
	  placement="below" regardless of vertical position.  Placement is now
	  inferred from the sign of Pos: Pos >= 0 gives above, Pos < 0 gives below.
	  This fixes text directions such as "Slightly faster" (Pos:7) appearing
	  below the stave instead of above it.
	- Parser: StaffProperties EndingBar values such as "Section Close" were
	  stored verbatim with spaces, but _emit_measure compared against the
	  no-space forms ("SectionClose").  The mismatch caused the ending barline
	  to be silently dropped.  EndingBar values are now normalised (spaces
	  stripped) on ingestion.  Additionally, a second StaffProperties record
	  (carrying channel/volume data) was clobbering the EndingBar already
	  parsed from the first record; _ending_bar is now only updated when the
	  field is present in the record.

0.002.3	Mon Nov  2 02:09:55 PM EST 2026
	[ Bug Fixes ]
	- Parser/MusicXML: Tempo records with an optional Text field (e.g.
	  Text:"With Expression") were silently discarded.  The text is now stored
	  in the Tempo event and emitted as a <words font-style="italic"> direction
	  in the same <direction> block as the metronome mark.  When text is
	  present the metronome element uses parentheses="yes" so renderers display
	  the marking as e.g. "With Expression (crotchet = 92)".
	- MusicXML: TempoVariance style Ritenuto was emitted verbatim as "Ritenuto"
	  instead of the standard abbreviation "rit.".
	- t/edge_cases.t: permission-check subtest now skips on Cygwin where
	  chmod 0000 does not restrict file reads due to Windows ACL mapping.
	  fixes https://matrix.perl-magpie.org/results/b4259172-d4a0-11f1-b947-97e253e5423d

0.002.2	Fri Oct 30 04:14:18 PM EDT 2026
	[ Bug Fixes ]
	- Parser: NWCTXT files produced by some NWC versions spell the hairpin
	  dynamic record as DynamicVariance instead of the abbreviated DynVariance.
	  Added DynamicVariance as an alias in the dispatch table so crescendo,
	  diminuendo, and hairpin-off markings are parsed correctly from both spellings.

0.002.1	Mon Oct 12 04:14:34 PM EDT 2026
	[ Bug Fixes ]
	- NWC TempoVariance:Fermata records were emitted as a text direction
	  (<words font-style="italic">Fermata</words>) instead of the correct
	  MusicXML <fermata/> notation element on the decorated note or rest.
	  Fermata symbols now appear as <notations><fermata/></notations> on the
	  sounding event that immediately follows the TempoVariance:Fermata record.

0.002.0	Fri Oct  9 08:39:33 PM EDT 2026
	[ Bug Fixes ]
	- MusicXML::_annotate_events: slur_stop was placed on the last note carrying
	  the Slur token rather than on the landing note (the first following note
	  without Slur).  For the common single-note slur this produced a zero-length
	  arc with start and stop on the same note.
	- NWC::read: suppress autodie on the open() call so the "Cannot read file"
	  croak fires correctly on Cygwin, where -r returns true for chmod 0000 files
	  due to imprecise Windows ACL mapping.
	  fixes https://matrix.perl-magpie.org/results/dbc4dafe-7e31-1014-904b-aa3c0773776a
	[ Enhancements ]
	- Score::validate now performs per-staff checks when --validate is passed:
	  empty staff detection, measure-duration consistency against the active
	  time signature, unmatched tie detection, and unclosed slur detection.

0.001.0	Fri Sep 18 12:49:11 PM EDT 2026
      Initial CPAN release. Fully functional NWC-to-MusicXML conversion pipeline.

      Core modules:
      - Music::NWC2MusicXML         -- top-level facade; single-file and batch conversion.
      - Music::NWC2MusicXML::NWC    -- NWC 2.x binary container decoder (zlib decompression).
      - Music::NWC2MusicXML::Parser -- NWCTXT text parser producing Score/Staff/Event trees.
      - Music::NWC2MusicXML::Score  -- internal score model.
      - Music::NWC2MusicXML::Staff  -- internal staff model.
      - Music::NWC2MusicXML::Event  -- internal event model with exact rational durations.
      - Music::NWC2MusicXML::MusicXML -- MusicXML 4.0 generator.
      - Music::NWC2MusicXML::Diagnostics -- i18n warning/logging subsystem.
      - bin/nwc2musicxml            -- command-line interface.

      MusicXML features emitted:
      - Notes, chords, rests (all NWC durations; dotted, double-dotted, triplets).
      - Grace notes (<grace/> element; duration omitted per MusicXML schema).
      - Slurs (numbered 1-6 for simultaneous arcs), ties, articulations, ornaments.
      - Clef, key-signature, and time-signature changes (initial and mid-staff).
      - Transposing instruments (<transpose><chromatic>).
      - Tempo and tempo-variance directions (metronome, rit., accel., etc.).
      - Dynamic markings with per-staff MIDI velocity (DynVel) mapping.
      - Hairpin crescendo/diminuendo wedges.
      - Text directions, flow-control marks (coda, segno, D.C., D.S., Fine, ...).
      - Lyrics with syllabic type (begin/middle/end/single).
      - Part groups (bracket and brace) from WithNextStaff flags.
      - MIDI channel, program, volume, and pan from NWC staff properties.
      - Visible/hidden staves (print-object="no" on part-name).
      - Custom ending barlines from NWC EndingBar property.
      - Asymmetric page margins (Left/Right/Top/Bottom from PgMargins).
      - Word-font and lyric-font defaults from NWC Font records.
      - Score metadata: title, author, lyricist, copyright, comments.
      - Repeat barlines (MasterRepeatOpen/Close, LocalRepeatOpen/Close).
      - Double, section-close, and other barline styles.

      CLI features:
      - Single-file and batch conversion.
      - Recursive directory scanning (--recursive).
      - Selectable output directory (--output-dir).
      - Overwrite guard (--overwrite).
      - Warning log file (--warnings).
      - Extended consistency validation (--validate).

0.000030  2026-11-27 23:50:48-08:00 America/Los_Angeles
    - Complete rewrite, not compatible with earlier releases. Start with DBIx::QuickORM::Manual and its Quickstart.
    - Connect to PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, or DuckDB from a dbh, a connect sub, or credentials, with UTF-8 and time zone session setup.
    - Every connection runs with AutoCommit on, and the ORM manages transactions. SQLite connections get PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON.
    - The database is scanned into a map of tables, fields, and keys, adjusted by the autotype, types, fks, omit, default_fields, row_classes, row_namespace, and row_class_name arguments.
    - Types: DateTime, JSON, and UUID, chosen by declared type or by field name, plus custom types through DBIx::QuickORM::Role::Type, with format and generate field hints.
    - Typed primary key fields an insert leaves out get a value from their type (UUID: version 7).
    - CRUD operations: insert, insert_many, update_row, delete_row, refresh_row, find, find_or_insert, and vivify.
    - Rows: cached, inflated field reads with raw and inflated forms, plus update, delete, refresh, insert, cas_update, is_in_db, and follow_fk.
    - via => {field => field} follows, joins, or inserts along fields no foreign key in the map connects, wherever link is taken.
    - insert_fk and insert_many_fk, on the ORM and on rows, insert rows that point at a row, filling their foreign key fields from it.
    - The row cache holds one canonical copy of each row's data by primary key (typed keys match in any form): is_canon, clear_cache, retain_cache, and enforce_canon.
    - Handles over tables and SQL queries with chainable modifiers (where, order_by, limit, join, group_by, and more), readers (first, all, only, iter, count), and bulk update and delete.
    - Joined rows are DBIx::QuickORM::JoinRow objects, and computed rows are DBIx::QuickORM::AggregateRow objects.
    - set_enforce_canon and set_datetime_parsers change those settings on a live ORM, but the other settings are fixed at construction.
    - Background queries: async and aside on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB, and forked wherever a second connection works, but aside and forked are refused inside a transaction.
    - Transactions as an object or around a block, with savepoints, isolation levels, and retry => N for deadlocks and serialization failures. A failed statement marks its transaction failed: only a rollback can follow, and a commit croaks.
    - having may name a computed column on every database, and outside MySQL and MariaDB the column's SQL is written in its place.
    - Where clauses use SQL::Abstract syntax by default, with the raw, inflated, binary, and sql value markers and pluggable where builders.
    - Database errors are DBIx::QuickORM::Exception::DB objects, classified by kind, with a retriable flag.
    - DBIx::QuickORM::DSL gives orm, table, and row blocks, and DBIx::QuickORM::ORM builds an ORM from its orm block and table classes.
    - Manual pages with tested examples, including one for readers coming from DBIx::Class.

0.17  2026-11-27 23:38:46 JST
        - Keep reading psgi.input until the requested length, EOF or an

          psgi_header and psgi_redirect:

          newlines, and -set-cookie is accepted as a cookie alias
        - Document CGI.pm 5.02's request limits and other changes as they

0.11	2026-11-28
        - FREEZE and THAW. An object whose class has a FREEZE method is
          written as what FREEZE('Struct::Codec') returns, under the new tag
          0x39, and decoded by THAW('Struct::Codec', @values) on its class:
          the protocol of Types::Serialiser, CBOR::XS, Sereal and JSON::XS.
          It is how a pointer object is carried rather than refused or
          stripped, and how an object that keeps its state in C magic, as
          HAMT's containers do, is carried at all: before this one came back
          an empty shell with no error. Shared objects are thawed once; a
          cycle back into an object through its own FREEZE values is refused
          by name. Streams without such an object are unchanged.
        - For XS consumers: the ABI's encode, encode_to and decode call FREEZE
          and THAW as the Perl surface does, so an entry can run Perl code;
          sc_abi.h says so. The table is unchanged, at version 1.
        - FIXES a stream the encoder wrote that its decoder refused with
          "reference to a value that was not tracked": a tied scalar in two
          slots whose tie object was shared too. The scalar was registered
          after its tie object, out of the offset order the lookup searches.
        - FIXES canonical => 1 giving one hash's data different bytes when
          a key held a code point past 0x7FFFFFFF beside Latin-1 keys. Perl
          writes those in seven or thirteen bytes, the comparison read at
          most six, and the order it gave was not transitive.
        - FIXES a stream the encoder wrote that its decoder refused as a
          pointer object: an integer in a class with an XS DESTROY that
          perl had also cached as a float, as it does for an address once
          divided. It went out as the integer, so it is refused as one on
          encode, and strip_pointers drops it.
        - FIXES an object of class Regexp that is no regexp - bless {},
          'Regexp' - coming back unblessed, and a blessed scalar there
          being refused as "a Regexp with no pattern". A regexp is known by
          its type now, not by its class.

0.10	2026-10-21
        - canonical => 1 on struct_encode: every hash's keys in order, so
          equal data is equal bytes in any process.

0.09	2026-10-11
        - Builds on 5.10.0: HeUTF8 is defined where perl lacks it.

0.08	2026-09-20
        - t/34-pointers.t asked for 2**40 to be an integer, which it is not
          where ivsize is 4.

0.07	2026-09-19
        - A pointer object whose integer has been printed was encoded, not
          refused: before 5.36 perl marks the digits it caches as a string.
          A string that spells the integer back is the integer now, so the
          refusal is the same on every perl. A blessed decimal string used
          as a number has those flags too and is refused with it.

0.06	2026-09-19
        - Refuse a pointer object: a blessed integer scalar in a class with a
          DESTROY, on encode and on decode, so the copy's DESTROY never frees
          an address it does not own.
        - struct_encode takes strip_pointers => 1 to write such an object as
          undef instead.

0.05	2026-09-18
        - FIXES a heap corruption decoding a hash key of length zero that
          carries the UTF-8 flag. 
        - t/25-wide-nv.t used perl's numifier to build -1.797...e+308, which
          overflows to -Inf below 5.30, and an infinity compares against
          nothing. The exponent is divided out and the mantissa named.
        - t/14-corrupt.t asserted two refusals that only a 64-bit UV gives:
          an eleven-byte varint is refused for its width, not its length,
          where a UV is 32 bits, and the descriptor fixture is now a value
          past INT_MAX that still fits one.

0.04	2026-09-18
        - A float on a perl built -Dusequadmath kept one significant digit: a
          third came back 0.3, and on a 32-bit one perl died "panic:
          my_snprintf buffer overflow". The precision was passed as "%.*",
          which my_snprintf never hands to quadmath_snprintf. It is written
          into the format now, as perl's own sv.c does.
        - A float on a perl built -Duselongdouble below 5.30 came back a ULP
          or two out: the digits were read with Atof, which is perl's own
          numifier and was not correctly rounded until 5.30 (perl RT #41202).
          The decoder names strtold, strtoflt128 or strtod for the build.
        - Those digits now use '.' for a radix whatever the locale is.
        - t/25-wide-nv.t asserts the digit count on the bytes, and no longer
          uses perl's numifier as an oracle on a perl whose numifier is the
          thing at fault.

0.03	2026-09-17
        - FIXES a heap corruption when encoding an anonymous sub. The
          deparser is loaded with load_module, which runs perl and can
          reallocate the argument stack; the stack pointer taken before it
          was then stale, and pushing the deparse arguments through it wrote
          to freed memory. It surfaced only when the load triggered a
          realloc, so it depended on how deep the stack already was: a bare
          encode was usually fine and a sub encoded from inside a larger
          program crashed at destruction. SPAGAIN after the load. Seen as a
          SIGABRT/SIGSEGV in t/32-kinds.t on threaded 5.18.
        - t/16-leak.t built its probe list with a regexp unconditionally,

        - A float on a perl built -Duselongdouble or -Dusequadmath kept only

          under tag 0x38, and comes back the number it was. A perl whose NV
          is a double writes the same bytes as before.
        - t/25-wide-nv.t.

0.16  2026-11-28
     - Fix: extracted words and lines reported the descender line as the
       baseline. Words now carry baseline() and lines group by it.
     - Fix: text extraction read only files laid out the way PDF::Make
       writes them. It now reads other producers' PDFs.
     - Fix: /DecodeParms was ignored and a /Filter array decoded backwards.
     - Fix: a cross-reference stream not at offset 0 was misread.
     - Fix: a file with a /Prev chain opened only through the repair scan.
     - Fix: an object stream was inflated again for every object in it.
     - Fix: string escapes in a content stream were not decoded.
     - Fix: cm composed in the wrong order and glyph boxes ignored the CTM.
     - Fix: fonts, widths and descriptors behind references were not read.
     - Fix: a stated glyph width of 0 was replaced by a guess.
     - Fix: inline image data was parsed as content.
     - Fix: one long or empty mapping cut a ToUnicode map short.
     - Fix: the column pass split words and lines at a column boundary.
     - New: rotated text, right-to-left words, /ActualText, Type 3 widths.
     - New: Unicode for Adobe-Japan1, Korea1, KR, GB1 and CNS1 CIDs when a
       font has no ToUnicode map, from Adobe's tables (BSD 3-Clause).

0.15  2026-10-06
     - Fix: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH was ignored on Windows. 

0.14  2026-10-05
     - Fix: Font rendering incorrect family
     - Fix: pdfmake_font_write was a stub, a TTF carried no /BaseFont, and
       pdfmake_page_add_font rejects anything but a Standard 14 name.
       TrueType fonts now embed as a subsetted /Type0 font with Identity-H
       encoding, a /CIDToGIDMap stream and a /ToUnicode CMap, and a loaded
       font is usable as a font family. Reported by ULIBUCK.
     - Fix: PDF::Make::Font->from_file and from_bytes kept a pointer into a
       buffer they then released. Every cmap lookup, advance and subset read
       freed memory; it returned correct answers until the allocator reused
       the block, then glyph 0 for everything.
     - Fix: a single-column page with a large heading could be split by a
       phantom column gutter, reordering and splitting extracted words.
       A gutter now has to have text on both sides of it on more than one
       line.
     - Fix: Make.c did not depend on the xs/*.xs files Make.xs includes, so
       an edit to an XSUB rebuilt and relinked without taking effect.
     - New: PDF::Make::Page->add_font_ref, to name an existing font object
       in a page's resources.
     - New: PDF::Make::Canvas->Tj_hex, for composite-font glyph strings.

     - Fix: the backward scan for startxref compared the keyword from
       positions where fewer than nine bytes remained, reading past the end
       of the file buffer. Harmless slack on most allocators, a SIGSEGV on
       OpenBSD when the buffer ended on a page boundary.
     - Fix: the %PDF- version digits are parsed within the buffer, so a file
       whose digits run to EOF cannot walk off it.
